    博弈聚焦的端到端对手行为学习Game-Focused End-to-End Learning of Adversary Behavior

    End-to-End Game-Focused Learning of Adversary Behavior in Security Gamesin Security Games — full title

    Andrew PerraultBryan WilderEric EwingAditya MateBistra DilkinaMilind Tambe

    哈佛 CRCS × 南加州大学 CAIS · AAAI-20, pp. 1379–1386Harvard CRCS × USC CAIS · AAAI-20, pp. 1379–1386

    一句话定位：In one sentence: 在反盗猎巡逻问题中，预测盗猎者行为的模型不该按"预测得准"训练，而应该按"让巡逻队少受损失"端到端训练——数据越少，这个区别越致命。 In anti-poaching patrol planning, a model that predicts adversary behavior should not be trained to predict accurately — it should be trained end-to-end so that patrols lose less. The scarcer the data, the more this distinction matters.

    Decoding the title · 1/2

    "End-to-End"（端到端）到底是什么意思What "end-to-end" actually means

    标题第一刀切在 End-to-End 上。这个词来自深度学习工程，图景是一条流水线：原始输入从一端进入，最终业务结果从另一端流出。

    The first cut of the title is End-to-End. The term comes from deep-learning engineering and evokes a pipeline: raw input enters one end, the final business outcome flows out the other.

    raw data
    →
    model
    →
    decision / action
    →
    real-world outcome

    "非端到端"= 流水线被切成几段，每段独立优化。传统做法先训一个预测模型（这段的目标：预测准），再把预测交给下游环节使用（那段的目标：决策好）。两段的目标函数不一样——这就是全文攻击的裂缝。

    "Not end-to-end" = the pipeline is cut into stages, each optimized separately. The classical recipe trains a predictive model first (that stage's goal: predictive accuracy), then hands the prediction to a downstream consumer (whose goal: decision quality). The two stages optimize different objectives — that is the crack this paper attacks.

    "端到端" = 打通整条管线的梯度。让"最终业务结果有多好"这个信号，以梯度的形式从管线末端一路流回模型参数——模型训练时"知道"自己的预测会被如何使用。本站第 49 卡会把这条梯度通路画给你看。

    "End-to-end" = gradients flow through the whole pipeline. The signal "how good is the final outcome" is propagated, in the form of gradients, from the very end of the pipeline back into model parameters — so during training the model "knows" how its prediction will be used. Card 49 draws this gradient path for you.

    一行记忆：端到端不是"自动化程度高"，而是训练目标 = 最终目标。近义词：decision-focused learning（决策聚焦学习）、task-based learning。反义词：two-stage、predict-then-optimize。 One-line memory: end-to-end does not mean "more automation" — it means the training objective is the final objective. Synonyms: decision-focused learning, task-based learning. Antonyms: two-stage, predict-then-optimize.
    你可能会问：这个词和"端到端加密"是一回事吗？You might ask: same "end-to-end" as in end-to-end encryption?

    不是。加密里的"端到端"指通信两端之间不经过中间服务器；深度学习里的指训练信号贯穿整条管线。同一个形容词，两个行业两码事。

    No. In encryption it means no intermediaries between two communicating ends; in deep learning it means the training signal spans the whole pipeline. Same adjective, different trades.

    Decoding the title · 2/2

    Game-Focused、Adversary Behavior、Security GamesGame-Focused, Adversary Behavior, Security Games

    Game-focused（博弈聚焦）Game-focused

    "端到端"训到哪一端？本文的答案：训到博弈结果那一端。模型的学习目标不是"预测准"，而是"在这场博弈里防守方效用高"——损失函数由博弈的胜负定义，所以叫博弈聚焦。第 43 卡正式定义它。

    End-to-end up to which end? This paper's answer: all the way to the game's outcome. The model is trained not for predictive accuracy but for the defender's utility in the game — the loss is defined by the game, hence game-focused. Card 43 makes this precise.

    Adversary behavior learning（对手行为学习）Adversary behavior learning

    防守方的优化需要知道对手怎么反应，但对手的"行为模型"（什么诱导他攻击哪里）是未知的，只能从历史攻防记录里学出来。"学对手"本身就是本文的问题 Setting 的一半。

    The defender's optimization needs to know how the adversary responds — but the adversary's behavior model (what lures him to attack where) is unknown and must be learned from historical attack records. Learning the adversary is half of the paper's problem setting.

    Security games（安全博弈）Security games

    资源有限的防御者 vs 策略性攻击者的博弈模型，代表作是 Stackelberg 安全博弈（SSG）——机场安检巡逻、野生动物反盗猎、电网防护都用它。第 26–27 卡从零建立这个模型。

    Game models of a resource-limited defender vs a strategic attacker — the canonical form being Stackelberg security games (SSGs), used for airport patrols, wildlife anti-poaching, and power-grid protection. Cards 17–18 build this model from zero.

    标题全读法：The full title, read slowly: "端到端地、以博弈胜负为目标，学习安全博弈中对手的行为模型"——三个术语各占一个技术贡献：端到端（梯度贯穿）、game-focused（损失=效用）、adversary learning（学的是对手）。 "Learning the adversary's behavior model end-to-end, with the game's outcome as the training objective." Each term owns one technical contribution: end-to-end (gradients through), game-focused (loss = utility), adversary learning (what gets learned).
    Narrative · why this paper exists叙事场 · 为什么需要这篇论文

    锡雷诺克国家公园的夜晚A night in Srepok National Park

    想象你站在柬埔寨东北部锡雷诺克国家公园的边缘。天刚黑，热带的湿气贴在皮肤上。这片森林里住着全球不足百头的爪哇野牛、印度野牛，和一群把偷猎当生计的人。

    Picture yourself at the edge of Srepok National Park, northeastern Cambodia. Night is falling; tropical humidity clings to your skin. This forest holds fewer than a hundred wild cattle of two endangered species — and people who poach for a living.

    盗猎者的手段安静而致命：钢丝套索。套索布在兽径上，几天后来收，没人拆就永远等着。巡护员的工作就是赶在动物之前找到它们。

    The poachers' tool is quiet and lethal: wire snares. Set on animal trails, collected days later — and if nobody removes them, they wait forever. Rangers race the animals to find them first.

    论文图 1a：巡护员在锡雷诺克收缴的套索（原图）Paper Fig. 1a: snares removed by rangers in Srepok (original)

    但你的巡护队经费只够覆盖公园的一小角。几十上百个巡护格，十几支队伍。今晚，派去哪里？

    But your budget covers only a fraction of the park. A hundred-odd patrol zones, a dozen squads. Tonight — where do you send them?

    你手里有一叠历史数据You hold a stack of historical data

    过去几年，巡护员记录了每一次巡逻：去了哪、发现多少套索。数据会说话——盗猎者偏爱动物多的区域、避开巡护站附近、雨季旱季路线不同。于是问题变成：怎么用这些数据决定今晚的巡逻？

    For years rangers have logged every patrol: where they went, how many snares they found. The data speaks — poachers favor animal-dense zones, avoid stations, shift routes seasonally. So the question becomes: how do you turn this data into tonight's patrol plan?

    两派思路Two schools of thought

    第一派说：先学会预测盗猎者——训练模型把"每个区域被盗猎的概率"算准，再对着预测布防。这是全世界的标准做法，直觉上无懈可击。

    School one says: first learn to predict the poachers — train a model to get each zone's poaching probability right, then deploy against the prediction. This is the standard recipe worldwide, and intuitively airtight.

    第二派还没出现。带着一个问题往下读："预测得准"和"防守得好"，真的是同一件事吗？

    School two does not exist yet. Carry one question as you read on: is "predicting accurately" really the same thing as "defending well"?

    暂停 10 秒，认真想。如果你不确定——很好。这正是 2016 年前整个领域没想清楚的事。这篇论文会告诉你：它们不仅不同，有时候更准的模型让你输得更惨。 Pause ten seconds and think hard. Unsure? Good — so was the entire field before 2016. This paper will show they are not the same, and that sometimes the more accurate model defends worse.
    你可能会问：这是真实场景吗？You might ask: is this a real scenario?

    是。green security 框架（Fang, Stone & Tambe 2015）来自真实的反盗猎部署，数据是巡护系统记录的真实套索发现。人机博弈对抗盗猎 2010 年代就在柬埔寨、乌干达等多国野外运行。

    Yes. The green-security framework (Fang, Stone & Tambe 2015) came out of real anti-poaching deployments; the snare data is real ranger logs. Game-theoretic patrol planning has run in the field in Cambodia, Uganda and elsewhere since the 2010s.

    General theory · kp-expected-utility一般理论 · 知识点 kp-expected-utility

    期望效用：不确定世界的记账法Expected utility: bookkeeping for an uncertain world

    摆在你面前两个信封。红信封：打开必得 300 元。蓝信封：一半概率 700 元，一半概率什么都没有。规则只许挑一个。你挑哪个？

    Two envelopes. Red: open it, get 300, guaranteed. Blue: a coin toss — 700 or nothing. You may keep one. Which do you take?

    大多数人会算一笔账：蓝信封"平均"值多少？一半的时间 700，一半的时间 0——长期开下去，平均每次拿 350 元。350 > 300，所以理性账面上蓝信封更值。这个"长期平均值"就是本卡的全部主题：期望效用。它回答的问题 universal 到不能再 universal——当结果不确定时，一个选择到底"值多少"？

    Most people run the same little calculation: what is the blue envelope worth 'on average'? Half the time 700, half the time 0 — opened forever, it averages 350 per open. And 350 > 300, so on paper blue wins. That long-run average is this card's entire subject: expected utility. It answers a maximally universal question — when outcomes are uncertain, what is a choice actually worth?

    读法（三步）：①列出所有可能的结果 o；②每个结果记两个数——发生的概率 Pr(o) 和它的价值 U(o)；③全部相乘再相加。就这三步，没有更多。Read it in three steps: (1) list the outcomes o; (2) for each, note its probability Pr(o) and its value U(o); (3) multiply and add. That is all.

    再练一个（结果更多、有赔有赚）：一个游戏，50% 赚 40、25% 亏 20、25% 赚 10。值不值得玩？EU = 0.5×40 + 0.25×(−20) + 0.25×10 = 20 − 5 + 2.5 = +17.5。正的——玩得越多赚得越多；负的就要躲。注意亏的那项是负的效用：损失天然是负数。

    One more (more outcomes, gains and losses): a game pays +40 with probability 0.5, −20 with probability 0.25, +10 with probability 0.25. Play? EU = 0.5×40 + 0.25×(−20) + 0.25×10 = 20 − 5 + 2.5 = +17.5. Positive means each play earns on average; negative means run. Note the loss enters as a negative utility — losses are naturally negative.

    为什么叫"效用"而不叫"钱"？Why 'utility' rather than 'money'? 因为 U 度量的是这个决策者对结果的主观价值。同一张 100 元钞票：对身无分文的学生和对亿万富翁价值不同；疼一天、早下班一小时、一句道歉，也都能进效用。谁在做决策，就用谁的 U。记住这一条——后面你会看到攻击方和防守方对"同一批目标"各有一张完全不同的价值表，而期望效用对两边一视同仁。 Because U measures this decision-maker's subjective value of outcomes. The same 100-unit note is worth different things to a broke student and a billionaire; a day of pain, an hour saved, an apology — all can enter U. Whoever decides, their U is used. Hold onto this — later you will see attacker and defender holding completely different value tables for the same targets, while expected utility treats both sides identically.
    常见误解：Common misconception: 蓝信封"值 350"不是说"打开会得到 350"——那次打开只会是 700 或 0。期望不是任何一次的真实结果，是无数次重复的平均值。单次靠运气，长期看期望——这就是赌场永远赢的数学原因。 'The blue envelope is worth 350' does not mean an open yields 350 — that open is 700 or 0. The expectation is not any single outcome; it is the average over endless repetition. Single runs ride luck; the long run obeys the expectation — the mathematical reason casinos always win.
    你可能会问：那为什么还有人买"期望上亏钱"的保险和彩票？You might ask: why do people buy insurance and lottery tickets that lose on expectation?

    因为 U 不必等于钱。保险：花 500 消除"1% 概率损失 30 万"——期望上保险公司赚，但你买走了灾难可能性，你的 U 里"灾难"的负值远大于票面。彩票：花 2 元买一个"美梦的一线可能"，效用里有娱乐和希望的定价。期望效用框架完全容纳这些——只要 U 写得对。

    Because U need not equal money. Insurance: paying 500 to erase '1% chance of losing 300,000' — the insurer profits on expectation, but you bought away catastrophe, and in your U that tail is worth more than the premium. Lottery: 2 units buys a sliver of dream — hope is priced into U. The framework accommodates all of this, as long as U is written honestly.

    UNDERSTAND"这个决定期望效用是 350"的准确含义是？The precise meaning of 'this decision's expected utility is 350':

    APPLY数值题：50% 赚 40、25% 亏 20、25% 赚 10。EU = ?Numeric: +40 with probability 0.5, −20 with probability 0.25, +10 with probability 0.25. EU = ?

    TRANSFER迁移：两个求职 offer：A 公司月薪稳定 2 万；B 公司底薪 1 万 + 一半概率拿 3 万绩效。纯期望账面上谁赢？Transfer: two offers — firm A pays a steady 20k; firm B pays 10k plus a 50% chance of a 30k bonus. On pure expectation, who wins?

    本文如何用它：How this paper uses it: 下一卡：当对手会看你的招式，"随机"本身成为武器——混合策略。 Next card: when your opponent studies your pattern, randomness itself becomes a weapon — mixed strategies.
    In this paper · kp-expected-utility本文用法 · 知识点 kp-expected-utility

    期望效用：把运气平均掉Expected utility: averaging out luck

    上一卡（1a）是期望效用的一般理论：EU = Σ 概率×效用——任意结果集、任意主体。本文不需要全部的一般性，它只问一件事：站到防守方的立场上，这个定义会长成什么样子？这一卡就是推导过程。

    The previous card (1a) gave the general theory: EU = Σ Pr(o)·U(o) — any outcome set, any agent. This paper does not need all that generality. It asks one thing: from the defender's seat, what does the definition grow into? This card is that derivation.

    本文的公式：从一般定义推出来The paper's formula, derived from the general definition

    现在做第一次特化：站到防守方的立场（效用表 ud），只看一个哨点：60% 概率被造访、得手损失 100、覆盖则攻击必败。这个"小世界"里结果只剩两种——"攻击成功"（概率 (1−p)·q，防守方效用 −|ud|）和"其余一切"（效用 0）。代入一般定义，求和只剩一项：

    Now the first specialization: take the defender's seat (utility table ud) and watch a single post: visited with probability 0.6, damage 100 if the raid succeeds, covered means any attack fails. In this tiny 'world' only two outcomes remain — 'attack succeeds' (probability (1−p)·q, defender utility −|ud|) and 'everything else' (utility 0). Substitute into the general definition and the sum collapses to one term:

    p = 覆盖概率，q = 攻击概率，|ud| = 得手损失。习惯上把负的期望效用报告为正的"损失"——三个因子各管一件事：防不住 × 他要来 × 后果。p = coverage, q = attack probability, |ud| = damage. By convention the negative expected utility is reported as a positive 'loss' — one factor per question.

    划清界限：这里发生了两次特化，不是一个。Drawing the line: TWO specializations happened here, not one. ① 谁的效用？——防守方的（ud）。期望效用本身不偏袒任何一方：把同一定义套到攻击方身上，他打目标 i 的期望效用就是 ——正是第 29 卡理性对手 argmax 里的那个量。攻防双方用的是同一条定义、两张不同的效用表。② 什么场景？——防守视角、单哨点、二元结果。换到保险、投资、考试，结果集一变，公式长相就变——灵魂不变。第 27 卡的 DEU 只是放开了"单目标"这条限制，它仍然是防守方这一个主体的期望效用。 (1) Whose utility? — the defender's (ud). Expected utility itself favors no one: apply the same definition to the attacker and his expected utility from hitting target i is — precisely the quantity inside the rational attacker's argmax in card 29. Both sides live on one definition, with two different utility tables. (2) Which scenario? — defense, one post, binary outcomes. In insurance, investing, or exams the outcome set changes, and the formula's face changes with it — never its soul. DEU (card 27) merely drops the 'single target' restriction — yet it is still the expected utility of one single agent: the defender.

    拖动覆盖率 p，点击"模拟 20 季"。先预测：p=50% 时 20 季里大概几个红点？Drag coverage p, then simulate 20 seasons. Predict first: at p = 50%, roughly how many red dots?
    0%
    Expected loss = (1−p) × 0.6 × 100 =期望损失 = (1−p) × 0.6 × 100 = 60.0
    常见误解：Common misconception: 期望损失 60 不是"最可能的结果是 60"。单季只有 0 或 100 两种——期望是大量重复后的平均值。 An expected loss of 60 does not mean "60 is the most likely outcome". A single season gives 0 or 100 only — the expectation is the average over many repetitions.
    你可能会问：为什么用损失（负收益）？You might ask: why losses (negative utility)?

    安全领域的习惯：攻击得手防守方受损，失败双方得 0。论文里 ud : T → ℝ≤0，防守的目标就是让期望损失趋近 0。

    Security convention: if the attack succeeds the defender suffers; if it fails both get 0. The paper's ud : T → ℝ≤0, and the defender's job is pushing expected loss toward 0.

    General theory · kp-mixed-strategy一般理论 · 知识点 kp-mixed-strategy

    混合策略：被看穿的代价Mixed strategies: the price of being read

    你和朋友玩石头剪刀布玩了一下午，输得莫名其妙。复盘才发现：你每次紧张时都出剪刀。朋友早就发现了，只是每次都静静等着收割你。你的失败不在于"猜错"，在于有模式，且模式被读走了。

    You lost all afternoon at rock-paper-scissors. The replay shows why: whenever nervous, you threw scissors. Your friend spotted it long ago and quietly harvested you. You didn't fail by guessing wrong — you failed because you had a pattern, and the pattern was read.

    补救方案有两种。差的方案："我以后随便出。"——"随便"通常也是模式（人自以为的随机里全是偏见）。好的方案：按一个精心选定的概率分布出招——比如各 1/3。这就是混合策略：不是"随便"，而是"按解出来的配方随机"。

    Two remedies. The bad one: 'I'll just play whatever' — 'whatever' is still a pattern (human 'randomness' is full of bias). The good one: play according to a carefully chosen probability distribution — say, thirds of each. That is a mixed strategy: not 'whatever', but 'random by prescription'.

    为什么 1/3 均匀是"不可剥削"的？自己验算：对手无视你、恒出石头。你均匀出招：出布赢（+1，概率 1/3）、出石头平（0，1/3）、出剪刀输（−1，1/3）→ 期望 = 1/3 − 1/3 = 0。对手换任何固定招，结果都是 0。对手再也占不到便宜——这就是"配方"的目标：让对手的任何应对都拿不到正收益。

    Why is uniform 1/3 'unexploitable'? Verify by hand: the opponent stubbornly plays rock while you mix uniformly: paper wins (+1, probability 1/3), rock ties (0, 1/3), scissors loses (−1, 1/3) → expectation = 1/3 − 1/3 = 0. Any fixed counter-move gives the same 0. The opponent can no longer profit — that is the prescription's goal: flatten every counter-strategy's expected gain.

    常见误解：Common misconception: "混合 = 随机乱出。"配方 (0.8, 0.1, 0.1) 和 (1/3, 1/3, 1/3) 是两个不同的策略——前者可以被针对性剥削。分布的形状本身就是策略内容，它是一道"让对手无机可乘"的优化题的解。 'Mixed = playing carelessly.' The prescription (0.8, 0.1, 0.1) and (1/3, 1/3, 1/3) are different strategies — the first is exploitable. The distribution's shape IS the strategy, the solution of an optimization that denies the opponent any edge.
    你可能会问：现实中人真的会按比例随机吗？You might ask: do humans really mix by the numbers?

    职业级会接近（点球大战的射门/扑救比例与理论预测惊人吻合），业余级会跑偏（随机序列里全是模式）。"想随机但随不好"不是笑话——它正是行为模型（下一篇论文的主力）研究的真实人性。

    Professionals come close (penalty-kick shooter/keeper ratios match theory remarkably); amateurs drift (their 'random' sequences crawl with patterns). 'Wanting to randomize but doing it badly' is not a joke — it is exactly the human nature that behavioral models (the next paper's workhorse) study.

    In this paper · kp-mixed-strategy本文用法 · 知识点 kp-mixed-strategy

    混合策略与覆盖概率Mixed strategies and coverage probability

    3 支巡逻队、8 个区域。固定巡同样的 3 个，盗猎者两周摸清规律。所以防守要随机化 (randomize)——这就是混合策略 (mixed strategy)。

    Three patrol squads, eight zones. Patrol the same three every week and poachers learn the pattern in two weeks. Defense must randomize — that is a mixed strategy.

    关心长期频率而非某一天：对每个目标 i 定义边际覆盖概率 (marginal coverage)：

    We care about long-run frequencies, not any single day. For each target i define the marginal coverage probability:

    8 区域、3 队 → 总预算 Σpi = 3。可以平均（每处 0.375），可以死守 3 个重点（1,1,1,0,…），最优解通常在两者之间——形状取决于对手口味。

    8 zones, 3 squads → budget Σpi = 3. Spread evenly (0.375 each) or harden three (1,1,1,0,…); the optimum usually lies between, and its shape depends on the adversary's tastes.

    常见误解：Common misconception: pi = 0.5 不是"有一半把握防住一次进攻"，而是长期时间频率——约一半时间处于被覆盖状态。期望损失公式里的 (1−pi) 乘的是"攻击发生时恰好没被防住"的概率。 pi = 0.5 is not "a 50% chance of blocking any given attack" — it is a long-run time frequency: covered about half the time. In the loss formula, (1−pi) is the probability an attack, when it comes, lands uncovered.
    你可能会问：为什么不直接排一张固定班表？You might ask: why not just fix a schedule?

    任何固定班表都会被看穿。混合策略把"不可预测性"本身变成防守资源——对手最多知道频率，猜不中下一次抽样。论文假设对手知道 p 并按自己的模型回应。

    Any fixed schedule gets learned. A mixed strategy makes unpredictability itself a defensive resource — the adversary knows at most the frequency, never the next draw. The paper assumes the adversary knows p and responds via his own model.

    General theory · kp-stackelberg-game一般理论 · 知识点 kp-stackelberg-game

    Stackelberg 博弈：先亮牌的人Stackelberg games: the player who shows first

    两家奶茶店在同一条街上选址。新店（后进入者）有个巨大便利：它可以先看看老店开在哪，再决定自己开在哪。老店掌柜若是有经验，选位置时会怎么办？——他会先想清楚："如果我在 A 处，对方会来 B 处对垒；如果我在 C 处，对方多半避开……"然后专挑'对方最优应对之下，我自己结果最好'的那个位置。

    Two tea shops choose locations on the same street. The new shop enjoys a huge convenience: it can look at where the old shop sits, then choose. An experienced old owner thinks ahead: 'If I open at A, they will answer at B; if at C, they will likely keep away…' Then she picks precisely the location that is best for herself given the other's best response.

    这个结构叫 Stackelberg 博弈（经济学家 von Stackelberg, 1934）：leader 先公开亮牌并定死，follower 看清后最优响应。奶茶店的智慧是它的全部精髓：既然对方必然针对你做最优反应，你就要在选招时把他的反应"算进去"——你不是在下自己的棋，是在下两个人的棋。

    This structure is a Stackelberg game (economist von Stackelberg, 1934): the leader moves first, publicly and irrevocably; the follower observes and best-responds. The tea-shop wisdom is its essence: since the opponent will surely best-respond to you, factor that response into your own choice — you are playing both sides of the board.

    解法叫"逆向归纳"：从最后一手往回想。先答"若 leader 出 X，follower 怎么应？"把每个选项下 follower 的响应都写下来，leader 挑响应后自己收益最高的那个。举个 4 字棋（收益记作 leader, follower）：leader 出 U → follower 在 (4,2) 与 (2,1) 中选自己高的，得 2 → leader 得 4；leader 出 D → follower 在 (1,3) 与 (2,3) 中选 3 → leader 得 1。比较：U 的 4 > D 的 1 → 亮 U，拿 4。

    The method is backward induction: reason from the last move. First answer 'given leader plays X, how does the follower respond?' for every X; then the leader picks the choice whose response favors her most. Mini-game (payoffs as leader, follower): leader plays U → follower chooses between (4,2) and (2,1), takes 2 → leader gets 4; leader plays D → follower chooses between (1,3) and (2,3), takes 3 → leader gets 1. Compare: U's 4 beats D's 1 → play U, earn 4.

    亮牌要"亮得死"：The reveal must be binding: 整套优势建立在 follower 相信你不会变上。口头保证不算数；烧掉自己的船、把排班写成公开制度、签下违约金——这些"断自己后路"的动作才让承诺可信。承诺不可信 = 博弈退化成同时出招 = 优势蒸发。 The whole advantage rests on the follower believing you won't switch. Verbal assurance doesn't count; burning your ships, publishing the schedule, signing penalties — self-binding moves make commitment credible. An incredible commitment degrades the game to simultaneous moves, and the advantage evaporates.
    诚实标注：先手不总占优。Honest note: first isn't always better. "先亮牌 = 赢"不是普适定理——某些定价博弈里先亮牌反而被后手杀价。优势取决于博弈的结构。所以每个新领域都必须重新推导一遍——这篇论文做的正是这件事。 'First = win' is not universal — in some pricing games revealing first invites undercutting. The advantage depends on the game's structure. Every new field must re-derive it — which is exactly this paper's job.

    In this paper · kp-stackelberg-game本文用法 · 知识点 kp-stackelberg-game

    Stackelberg 博弈：先出手的一方Stackelberg games: the first mover

    石头剪刀布是同时出招。安全博弈不同——它是先后手的：

    Rock-paper-scissors is simultaneous. Security is different — it is a sequential-move game:

    第一步 · 防守方（leader 领导者）Step 1 · Defender (leader)：确定巡逻方案并长期执行: commit to a patrol pattern and execute it long-term
    第二步 · 对手（follower 跟随者）Step 2 · Adversary (follower)：观察规律，针对性选择攻击目标: observe the pattern, choose where to attack accordingly

    这个结构叫Stackelberg 博弈（得名于经济学家 Heinrich von Stackelberg）。核心洞察：承诺本身就是力量——既然对手必然对你的策略做最优反应，你就能在制定策略时把他的反应算进去：你在替两个人做决策。

    This structure is a Stackelberg game (after economist Heinrich von Stackelberg). Its core insight: commitment is power — since the adversary will best-respond to your strategy anyway, you can factor his response into your own optimization. You are choosing for two players.

    盗猎者看不到巡逻文件，但不需要看：混合策略是长期频率，几个月足以感知"东区没人巡"。leader 承诺的不是某次路线，而是概率模式。

    Poachers never see patrol files — and need not: a mixed strategy is a long-run frequency, and months suffice to feel "the east zone is never patrolled". The leader commits to a probabilistic pattern, not a single route.

    为什么先手不吃亏？Why isn't moving first a disadvantage? 后出手的人才要"猜"。先承诺且对方必然适应你——等于你在优化一个"包含对手最优反应"的目标。论文里 DEU 的全部意义都建立在这个结构上。 The second mover is the one who must guess. Commit first, and the adversary adapts to you — so you optimize an objective that already contains his best response. Everything DEU means later rests on this structure.
    你可能会问：现实中谁先谁后怎么界定？You might ask: who is 'first' in reality?

    看谁在重复互动中先定下模式。排班是防守方定的、长期稳定；盗猎者随时可观察后行动——防守方是 leader。论文的历史覆盖 phistorical 就是防守方过去的"承诺"，攻击记录是对它的"回应"。

    Ask who fixes their pattern first in the repeated interaction. Patrol schedules are set and stable; poachers observe then act — the defender leads. The paper's phistorical is exactly the defender's past commitment, and the attack logs are the response.

    General theory · kp-softmax-qr一般理论 · 知识点 kp-softmax-qr

    Softmax：从"打分"到"出手概率"Softmax: from scores to choice probabilities

    先看两个人。小 A 面对两份工作，写下利弊清单反复权衡——但他最终的选择，连自己都说不准；每次遇到同样的局面，他大概率选心头好的那份，偶尔也会冲动选另一份。小 B 是个纯理性机器：永远选分数高的，绝不含糊。

    Meet two choosers. A faces two jobs, weighs lists endlessly — yet even he can't predict his own choice: he takes the better one most of the time, and occasionally the other. B is a pure rational machine: always the higher score, no wobble.

    怎么把"大概率选好的、偶尔选差的"写成数学？给每个选项算一个分数 si，然后按分数的指数分配选择概率：

    How to write 'mostly the good one, occasionally not' in math? Give each option a score si, then split choice probability by the exponential of scores:

    si = 选项的分数；λ = "较真程度"旋钮。指数的功能：把"分数差"放大成"概率差"。si = option score; λ = the 'seriousness' dial. The exponential's job: amplify score gaps into probability gaps.

    旋钮的两端 + 中间：λ = 0：所有选项概率相等（闭眼选）；λ 极大：几乎全押最高分（小 B）；有限的 λ 就是小 A——通常对、偶尔错，而且错的频率由分数差决定：两选项分数差 Δ，概率比恰好是 （差 1 → 约 2.7 倍；差 2 → 约 7.4 倍）。

    Both ends and the middle: λ = 0: all options equal (eyes closed); λ huge: nearly all-in on the top score (that's B); finite λ is A — usually right, occasionally wrong, with error rates set by score gaps: two options a gap Δ apart have probability ratio (gap 1 → about 2.7×; gap 2 → about 7.4×).

    这个形状你在两个领域都会遇到，名字不同：机器学习叫它 Softmax——分类网络的最后一步、大语言模型选词时的"温度"（低温=近小B，高温=更随机）、注意力权重，全是它；行为经济学叫它量化响应 (QR, McKelvey & Palfrey 1995)——描述"人类的选择是系统的、但不是完美的"。

    You will meet this shape in two fields under two names: machine learning calls it Softmax — the last layer of classifiers, the 'temperature' of LLM sampling (low = B-like, high = wilder), attention weights — all of it; behavioral economics calls it quantal response (QR, McKelvey & Palfrey 1995) — 'human choice is systematic, but not perfect'.

    常见误解：Common misconception: "Softmax 输出的 0.9 就是'九成把握'。"不一定——它只是分数变换后的相对份额，模型可以长期输出 0.9 而只有七成对（校准问题）。把它当合法的概率分配机制理解最准确；"置信度"的解读需要额外验证。 'A Softmax 0.9 means 90% sure.' Not necessarily — it is a relative share from score transformation; a model can output 0.9 forever while being right 70% of the time (calibration). Read it as a mechanism making scores into a legal distribution; 'confidence' requires separate validation.

    有限理性：QR 与 SoftmaxBounded rationality: QR and Softmax

    "完全理性人"只攻击期望收益最大的目标。真实的人会算错、会怕、会偷懒。有限理性 (bounded rationality) 把"偶尔犯错"写进数学。最常用的量化响应 (Quantal Response, QR)：每个选项被选的概率正比于收益的指数——

    A perfectly rational attacker hits only the best payoff. Real people miscalculate, fear, cut corners. Bounded rationality writes "occasionally wrong" into the math. The workhorse is the Quantal Response (QR): each option's choice probability is proportional to the exponential of its payoff —

    Ui = 选项 i 的吸引力，λ = 理性程度。这个形状就是机器学习里的 Softmax。Ui = attractiveness of option i, λ = rationality level. This is exactly Softmax from machine learning.

    33%
    33%
    λ → 0：完全随机（各 1/3）。λ → ∞：退化为"只攻击最优目标"。λ → 0: uniform random (1/3 each). λ → ∞: degenerates to "attack only the best target".

    论文对 λ 很克制：λ 越大对手越接近理性。定理 3 会证明端到端优势在 λ→∞ 依然保持——"对手不是白痴"不是本文方法的前提，只是现实本身。

    The paper is careful with λ: larger λ, more rational adversary. Theorem 3 will show the end-to-end advantage survives λ→∞ — "the adversary is no fool" is not an assumption of the method, just of reality.

    你可能会问：为什么偏偏是 exp？You might ask: why the exponential, of all things?

    数学上 exp 相乘=指数相加，多因素叠加干净利落（SUQR 就靠它把覆盖惩罚和目标价值加起来）；统计上指数族是"已知均值时最不做额外假设"的分布；而且 Softmax 梯度极其友好——端到端训练全靠它。

    Multiplying exponentials adds exponents, so combining factors is clean (SUQR exploits this to add coverage penalty + target value); the exponential family is maximally non-committal given the mean; and Softmax gradients are beautifully well-behaved — end-to-end training depends on that.

    主观效用：人心怎么给世界标价Subjective utility: how people price the world

    两件小事暴露同一个真相。事一：捡到 100 元的开心，远小于丢 100 元的肉疼。钱没变，感受变了。事二：口渴时第一杯水的价值远超第三杯——同一件东西，价值随你的处境变。

    Two little facts, one truth. Fact one: the joy of finding 100 is far smaller than the sting of losing 100. Same money, different feeling. Fact two: the first glass of water when thirsty beats the third — the same thing, valued differently by your situation.

    结论：人不是对"客观世界"做反应，而是对"自己感知到的世界"做反应。经济学给这个感知价值起了名字：主观效用。行为科学的任务，就是把"感知怎么偏离客观"系统地写成模型——比如前景理论说：人从参照点出发感知得失（先给你 100 再收回，你觉得是损失），且损失侧的感受更陡（损失厌恶）。

    Conclusion: people respond to the world as they perceive it, not as it objectively is. Economics names the perceived value subjective utility. Behavioral science's job is writing 'how perception departs from objectivity' into models — prospect theory, for one: gains and losses are felt relative to a reference point (given 100 then having it revoked reads as a loss), and the loss side is steeper (loss aversion).

    把"人心"装进公式的通用模板（本文的主角 SUQR 就是其一）：给每个选项算一个加法分数——"各项因素的加权贡献之和"，再交给 Softmax 变成概率：

    The universal template for putting 'the heart' into formulas (this paper's protagonist SUQR is one): compute each option's additive score — a weighted sum of factor contributions — and hand it to Softmax:

    f = 可测量的因素；w = 每个因素在人心里的"权重"（从数据里估）。加法的好处：因素之间互不纠缠，权重各有含义。f = measurable factors; w = each factor's psychological weight (estimated from data). Additive wins: factors don't tangle, and every weight keeps its meaning.

    三个工程理由：为什么全行业都用这个模板？Why the whole field uses this template: ①可估计：参数少，从行为数据里解得出来；②可分解：每个因素的贡献可以单独拎出来（下一篇论文的反演绝活全靠这一条）；③可解释：w 是负的就知道该因素是"劝退项"。模型不需要是人心的真相——它只需要在这个用途上够准。 (1) Estimable: few parameters, solvable from behavior; (2) decomposable: each factor's contribution lifts out cleanly (the next paper's inversion lives on this); (3) interpretable: a negative w tells you the factor repels. The model need not be the truth of the mind — only accurate enough for its use.
    常见误解：Common misconception: "主观 = 随便、不可研究。"恰恰相反——主观效用因人而异、因处境而异，但因此可以被数据逐人逐境地估计。"主观"是它敏感于个体处境的意思，不是它不可捉摸的意思。 'Subjective = arbitrary, unstudiable.' Quite the opposite — subjective utility varies by person and situation, and therefore can be estimated from data. 'Subjective' means it is indexed to individual circumstances, not that it is beyond study.

    SUQR：论文的主力对手模型SUQR: the paper's workhorse adversary model

    QR 说"按收益指数分配概率"，但没说收益是什么。SUQR (Subjective Utility QR，主观效用量化响应) 给出安全博弈里最常用的答案——把吸引力拆成两部分相加：

    QR says "probability ∝ exponential of payoff" but not what the payoff is. SUQR (Subjective Utility Quantal Response) gives the standard security-game answer — split attractiveness into two additive parts:

    • w · pi（覆盖惩罚）w · pi (coverage penalty)：w < 0 全局通用——覆盖越多越不吸引人。可提前用 MLE 学出（见图 1b，收敛很快）: w < 0, shared across targets — more coverage, less attractive. Learnable in advance by MLE (Fig 1b shows fast convergence)
    • φ(yi)（目标价值函数）φ(yi) (target value function)：输入目标 i 的特征向量 yi（动物数量、离站距离、地形……），输出天生多诱人。难学、必须从数据估——全文聚焦在学 φ: takes target i's feature vector yi (animal density, distance to station, terrain…) and outputs intrinsic attractiveness. Hard to learn, must be estimated from data — the paper's true battleground
    为什么不揉成一个网络？Why not one big network for everything? w 有清晰全局含义、跨博弈稳定、单独估计又快又准；φ 是每个目标的"个性"。把简单部分摘出来固定，复杂部分留给模型——论文原话：w 可用现有技术轻松学出并迁移，所以聚焦 φ。 w has a crisp global meaning, transfers across games, and is estimated fast; φ is each target's "personality". Factor out the easy part, reserve model capacity for the hard part. The paper says this directly: w is easy, so the effort goes to φ.
    常见误解：Common misconception: φ(yi) 不是盗猎者的"收益"，只是吸引力的一个分量；真正的概率还要过 exp 和归一化。两个目标吸引力差一个常数，攻击概率完全不变——这个小性质在第 47 卡反演 φ 时变成关键武器。 φ(yi) is not the poacher's "payoff", just one additive component; probabilities still pass through exp and normalization. A constant offset between two targets changes nothing about attack probabilities — a small fact that becomes the key weapon in card 47's inversion.
    你可能会问：特征 y 里都有什么？You might ask: what goes into the features y?

    合成实验每目标 100 维随机特征；人类数据实验 4 个经典特征：攻击者得手收益、防守方被得手损失、攻击者被抓损失、防守方抓到奖励。真实系统还会加动物密度、水源距离、历史巡逻强度。

    Synthetic experiments: 100 random features per target. Human-subject experiments: 4 classic features — attacker reward, defender penalty (on success), attacker penalty, defender reward (on failure). Real systems add animal density, water distance, patrol history.

    General theory · kp-loss-function一般理论 · 知识点 kp-loss-function

    损失函数：给"错"定一条计分规则Loss functions: a scoring rule for 'wrong'

    两位老师批同一份卷子，两位的评分哲学完全不同。张老师只判对错：对得满分，错得零分。李老师按步骤给分：方向对了给一半，算错数扣两分。一个月后，两位老师的学生的卷面分数可能一样，但他们的学习方法会完全不同——张老师的学生背题型，李老师的学生懂推理。

    Two teachers grade the same exam with opposite philosophies. Ms. Zhang grades right/wrong only: full or zero. Mr. Li awards partial credit: half for the right approach, minus two for arithmetic slips. A month later their classes may post identical scores — but they learned differently: Zhang's students memorize templates, Li's understand reasoning.

    机器学习模型就是张老师和李老师手下的学生。损失函数就是评分规则：模型的每次预测，按规则得一个分数（分数越低越好），模型的一切学习都围绕"把分数压下去"。你选了评分规则，就选定了学生成为什么样。

    An ML model is a student under such a teacher. The loss function is the grading rule: every prediction earns a score (lower is better), and all learning revolves around pushing it down. Choose the rule, and you have chosen what kind of student your model becomes.

    三种最常见的评分规则The three most common rules

    规则一 · 平方误差（MSE）——"偏差平方后记账"。预测房价 300、真实 320：记 (300−320)² = 400。平方让大错被重罚（差 10 记 100，差 20 记 400——错一倍罚四倍），所以模型会拼命避免离谱预测；代价是对个别极端样本过敏。

    Rule 1 · squared error (MSE) — square the deviation. Predict 3.0M, truth 3.2M: score (300−320)² = 400. Squaring punishes big misses disproportionately (off by 10 → 100; off by 20 → 400 — double the error, quadruple the fine), so the model avoids absurd predictions; the price is sensitivity to a few extreme samples.

    规则二 · 绝对误差（MAE）——"偏差直接记账"。同样例子记 |300−320| = 20。错多少记多少，不放大——对极端样本泰然处之；代价是"接近正确"和"差一点"在它眼里一样宽。

    Rule 2 · absolute error (MAE) — take the deviation as-is. Same example: |300−320| = 20. Errors count at face value, unamplified — calm about outliers; the price is treating 'close' and 'slightly off' identically.

    规则三 · 交叉熵——给"信心分配表"记账（上一卡的主角，用于输出概率的分类任务）。同一份预测、不同规则、不同分数——规则之间没有普对的，只有"对当前任务讲道理的"。

    Rule 3 · cross-entropy — scoring confidence tables (last card's protagonist, for tasks outputting probabilities). Same prediction, different rules, different scores — no universally right rule, only rules reasonable for the task.

    一个几乎所有 ML 项目都栽过的坑：A pit almost every ML project has fallen into: 评分规则是真实目标的代理。你真想要的往往是"模型在世界上表现好"，但你手里能优化的只有"训练集上分数低"。两者对不齐时，分数越漂亮、真实世界越糟。这个现象有名字：Goodhart 定律——"当一个测度变成目标，它就不再是好测度"。这篇论文的全部起点，就是发现安全博弈领域的标准损失和真实目标严重错位。 The scoring rule is a proxy for the real goal. What you truly want is 'the model does well in the world', but all you can optimize is 'low score on the training set'. When they misalign, prettier scores mean a worse world. It has a name: Goodhart's law — 'when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.' This whole paper begins by discovering that security games' standard loss is badly misaligned with the real goal.
    常见误解：Common misconception: "分数低 = 模型好。"只在评分规则与真实目标对齐时成立。训练分漂亮而真实表现糟糕的情形（过拟合、代理错位、刷指标）在业界俯拾皆是。永远追问一句：这条规则，真的在为我想要的东西打分吗？ 'Low score = good model.' True only when the rule aligns with the real goal. Beautiful training scores with bad real-world performance (overfitting, misalignment, metric gaming) are everywhere. Always ask: is this rule actually scoring what I want?
    你可能会问：损失函数是谁定的？能随便换吗？You might ask: who picks the loss? Can I swap it freely?

    建模者定的，而且能换——换损失不是技术细节，是立场声明。本文的核心论点正是"这个领域选错了损失"。换损失 = 告诉模型"什么才算错"，是它能收到的最高指令。

    The modeler picks it — and yes, it can be swapped: changing a loss is not a technicality, it is a statement of purpose. This paper's core claim is precisely that the field picked the wrong one. Changing the loss tells the model what actually counts as wrong — the highest directive it can receive.

    In this paper · kp-loss-function本文用法 · 知识点 kp-loss-function

    损失函数：给"错得有多离谱"定一个数Loss functions: turning 'how wrong' into a number

    机器学习训练的第一块基石：损失函数 (loss function)——把模型的预测和真实答案放进同一个公式，吐出一个非负数：预测越准数越小。训练的全部目标就是把它压下去。

    The first cornerstone of ML training: a loss function — put the model's prediction and the true answer into one formula, get out a non-negative number: the better the prediction, the smaller the number. All of training is pushing it down.

    两个最常见的例子（自己算一遍，每个都简单）：

    Two classics — compute both yourself, they are easy:

    • 平方误差 (MSE)Squared error (MSE)：预测房价 300 万、真实 320 万 → 误差 (300−320)² = 400。用于回归（连续值）: predicted 3.0M vs true 3.2M → (3.0−3.2)² = 0.04. For regression (continuous values)
    • 交叉熵 (cross-entropy)Cross-entropy：预测"是猫的概率 0.9"、真实是猫 → −log 0.9 ≈ 0.105。用于分类（概率分布）。下一卡专讲: predicted P(cat) = 0.9, truth is cat → −log 0.9 ≈ 0.105. For classification (probability distributions). Next card is devoted to it.
    为什么"非负"重要？Why does non-negativity matter? 损失要能跨样本相加比较。若正负可抵，"这题+10 那题−10"会伪装成零损失。非负保证"平均损失小"真的意味着"普遍预测得好"。 Losses must add up comparably across examples. If errors could cancel, "+10 here, −10 there" would masquerade as zero loss. Non-negativity guarantees "small average loss" really means "good predictions across the board".
    常见误解：Common misconception: 损失小 ≠ 准确率高。损失是对"整张概率分布"打分：预测 0.6 而真实发生，交叉熵只有 0.51，但按"只看最高概率"算它"答对"。损失关心你给了真相多少概率，不是你押对了没有。本文后面会利用这一点做文章。 Low loss ≠ high accuracy. A loss scores the whole predicted distribution: predicting 0.6 on something true costs only 0.51 in cross-entropy even though a "top-1" reading counts it wrong. The loss cares how much probability you gave the truth, not whether you guessed right. The paper will exploit exactly this later.
    你可能会问：损失函数是谁选的？能不能随便换？You might ask: who picks the loss? Can I swap it freely?

    人选的，而且本文的核心论点就是"选错了"——两阶段方法用交叉熵（预测的损失），而问题真正要的是效用（决策的损失）。换损失不是技术细节，是立场声明。这正是 20 年来 decision-focused learning 这条线的起点。

    Humans pick it — and this paper's whole point is that the field picked the wrong one: two-stage uses cross-entropy (a prediction loss) where the real goal is utility (a decision loss). Swapping a loss is not a technicality; it is a statement of purpose. That is where 20 years of decision-focused learning began.

    General theory · kp-cross-entropy一般理论 · 知识点 kp-cross-entropy

    交叉熵：给"自信的错"定罪Cross-entropy: sentencing confident mistakes

    想象你的朋友是天气预报员。整整一周，他每天都说"降水概率 10%"——结果下了一周雨。周五你去找他算账。他会辩解："我没有说一定不下啊，我给了 10% 的概率。"

    Imagine your friend is a weather forecaster. For a whole week he said '10% chance of rain' every day — and it rained all week. On Friday you confront him. He protests: 'I never said it wouldn't rain. I gave it 10%.'

    你觉得"错"字不够用。他不是没猜对——他是自信地错。另一个同事那一周都说"降水概率 60%"，也错了，但你对他没什么火气。同样都"错"，你心里给两个人记的账不一样。交叉熵就是把这笔账算清楚的记账规则。

    You feel 'wrong' is not enough. He didn't merely fail — he was confidently wrong. A colleague kept saying '60% chance of rain' all week and was wrong too, but you hold no grudge against him. Same outcome, different ledgers. Cross-entropy is the accounting rule that settles this ledger.

    积木一：模型输出的是一张"信心分配表"Block 1: a model outputs a confidence table

    先把词汇降到零。假设明天只有两种可能：晴、雨。一个人对明天的"信心"可以写成两张数字：

    First, strip the vocabulary. Suppose tomorrow has only two possibilities: sunny, rainy. A person's confidence about tomorrow is two numbers:

    晴Sunny雨Rain加起来Sum
    朋友（自信版）Your friend (confident)0.90.11.0
    同事（谦虚版）The colleague (humble)0.60.41.0

    每一行就是一张信心分配表：把"信心总额 1"分配给各种可能，加起来必须恰好等于 1（不允许留私房钱）。当一台机器"预测明天"时，它输出的就是这样一张表。机器学习的术语把这张表叫"概率分布"——名字唬人，本质就是一行加起来等于 1 的信心数字。

    Each row is a confidence table: the total confidence 1 is split among the possibilities and must sum to exactly 1 (no pocketing slack). When a machine 'predicts tomorrow', it outputs exactly such a table. ML jargon calls it a 'probability distribution' — an intimidating name for one row of confidence numbers summing to 1.

    积木二：给"稀罕程度"记账——log 出场Block 2: scoring rarity — enter the logarithm

    现在设计罚分规则。第二天真相揭晓——假设下雨了。对你朋友那张表（他给"雨"只留了 0.1 的信心），记多少分？我们的直觉要求：你给真相的信心越少，罚得越狠，而且狠得不成比例——给 0.1 的信心错了，应该比给 0.5 的信心错了惨好几倍，而不是多一点。

    Now design the scoring rule. Next day the truth is out — suppose it rained. How do we score your friend's table (he gave 'rain' only 0.1)? Our intuition demands: the less confidence you gave the truth, the harsher the penalty — disproportionately so. Being wrong at 0.1 should hurt several times worse than at 0.5, not slightly.

    有个绝妙的直觉把这件事自动化：你给真相的信心是 p，就相当于宣布"平均要试 1/p 次才对一次"。给雨 0.5 的信心 = "两次里对一次"；给雨 0.1 = "十次里才对一次"。数学里的 （对数）恰好把"试多少次才对"变成一个可以加减的分数：

    A beautiful intuition automates this: giving the truth confidence p amounts to declaring 'on average, 1/p attempts per success.' Confidence 0.5 on rain = 'right once in two tries'; 0.1 = 'once in ten.' The arithm turns 'tries per success' into a number you can add and compare:

    你给真相的信心 pConfidence p you gave the truth0.90.50.10.01
    相当于Equivalent to1.1 次对一次1.1 tries per hit2 次2 tries10 次10 tries100 次100 tries
    罚分 = −ln(p)Penalty = −ln(p)0.110.692.304.61

    看这张表的形状：信心从 0.9 掉到 0.5，罚分从 0.11 涨到 0.69（温和）；从 0.1 掉到 0.01，罚分从 2.30 飙到 4.61（翻倍再翻倍）。你朋友的"10% 信心错了"一天记 2.3 分——七天就是 16 分；谦虚的同事每天记 0.51 分。这笔账，终于和你心里的火气一样大了。

    Look at the shape: confidence dropping 0.9 → 0.5 moves the penalty 0.11 → 0.69 (gentle); 0.1 → 0.01 explodes it 2.30 → 4.61 (doubling and doubling again). Your friend racks up 2.3 per wrong day — 16 for the week; the humble colleague only 0.51 per day. The ledger finally matches your anger.

    为什么偏偏是 log，不是平方不是别的？Why the log specifically? 因为独立的事要加账。"周一的天气"和"周二的天气"是两件独立的事，总罚分应该等于两天之和。log 有个独家性质：相乘的事件，罚分相加（一周连对七天 = 罚 7×单日，不是别的怪数）。平方函数做不到这一点——它是为"连续值偏差"设计的，不是为"信心"设计的。 Because independent events must add up. Monday's weather and Tuesday's weather are independent; the total penalty should be the sum. The log has a unique property: events that multiply get penalties that add (seven days in a row costs exactly 7× one day). Squaring cannot do this — it was designed for continuous deviations, not for confidence.

    积木三：从"一件事的罚分"到"一整张表的总账"Block 3: from one event's penalty to the whole table's ledger

    上面的罚分只处理"一件事发生了"（那场雨）。但一张信心表给所有可能结果都分了信心，怎么打总分？答案符合常识：按"哪个结果真的发生"的概率权重，取平均——经常发生的结果多算几次，几乎不发生的少算（但乘数是概率，所以永远不发生的项自动归零）。

    The penalty above scores one event (that rain). But a confidence table assigns confidence to every outcome — how to score the whole table? The commonsense answer: average over outcomes, weighted by how often each really occurs — frequent outcomes count more; never-occurring ones drop out automatically (their weight is probability 0).

    把这个常识写成数学，就得到那个公式——现在你认识它的每一块了：

    Write that commonsense down and you get the formula — every piece is now familiar:

    q̂ = 被打分的信心表；q = "真相的权重表"（每个结果真实发生的比例）；−log(给真相的信心) = 单次罚分；Σ + qᵢ = 按真实频率把罚分平均。负号只是把"信心取 log 后的负数"翻成正数——账单要是正的。q̂ = the confidence table being scored; q = the truth's weights (how often each outcome really happens); −log(confidence given to truth) = the single-event penalty; the Σ with qᵢ averages penalties by true frequency. The minus sign only flips log's negatives positive — a bill must read positive.

    亲手算一遍：真值表 q = (1, 0)（这种天气必然是晴——比如在撒哈拉的七月）。朋友表 q̂ = (0.5, 0.5)。总账 = −(1×ln 0.5 + 0×ln 0.5) = −ln 0.5 ≈ 0.69。若朋友给晴 0.9：−ln 0.9 ≈ 0.11。同一片天空，账差六倍——给真相的信心就是一切。

    Compute one by hand: truth q = (1, 0) (this climate is always sunny — the Sahara in July). Friend's table q̂ = (0.5, 0.5). Ledger = −(1×ln 0.5 + 0) = −ln 0.5 ≈ 0.69. Had he said 0.9 on sunny: −ln 0.9 ≈ 0.11. Same sky, six-fold difference in the bill — confidence given to the truth is everything.

    常见误解：Common misconception: "账低 = 每次都猜对。"不是——账评的是整张信心表的质量。你给真相 0.6，账 0.51，虽然按"只看最高项"的标准你答对了。反过来给 0.99 而真相发生，账接近 0（答得又对又稳）。交叉熵衡量的是你有没有把信心放在真相那里，而不是你押中没有。 'A low bill = always guessing right.' No — it grades the whole table. Giving truth 0.6 costs 0.51 even though a top-1 reading calls it 'correct'; giving 0.99 when truth happens costs ≈0 (right and steady). Cross-entropy measures whether confidence sits where truth lives, not whether you hit the argmax.
    你可能会问：这些和"信息""熵"有什么关系？You might ask: what does this have to do with 'information' and 'entropy'?

    名字已经剧透了：−log(信心) 其实是"这条消息带来的信息量"（越不可能的事发生，信息越多）。交叉熵 = 用你的信心表去编码真相时平均付出的"比特数"。它和 KL 散度只差一个常数（真相自己的熵），所以"压低交叉熵"和"逼近真相分布"是同一件事。

    The name already spoils it: −log(confidence) is exactly the 'information content' of a message (the rarer the event, the more informative). Cross-entropy = the average bits you pay encoding truth with your confidence table. It differs from KL divergence by a constant (the entropy of truth), so 'minimizing CE' and 'approaching the true distribution' are the same task.

    UNDERSTAND下雨了。预报员甲事先给雨 0.2，预报员乙给雨 0.6。谁挨的罚重、重多少倍？It rained. Forecaster A had given rain 0.2; forecaster B gave it 0.6. Who pays more, and by what factor?

    APPLY数值题：真相必然是结果 2（q = (0, 1)），模型给 (0.75, 0.25)。CE = ?（三位小数，自然对数）Numeric: truth is certainly outcome 2 (q = (0, 1)); the model says (0.75, 0.25). CE = ? (3 decimals, natural log)

    本文如何用它：How this paper uses it: 下一卡：这篇论文用交叉熵给"盗猎者行为预测"打分——然后证明：这份账单打对了预测、打错了防守。 Next card: the paper uses cross-entropy to score its poacher-prediction — then proves the bill can score the prediction well and the defense badly.
    In this paper · kp-cross-entropy本文用法 · 知识点 kp-cross-entropy

    交叉熵：给整张概率分布打分Cross-entropy: scoring a whole distribution

    当模型输出的是概率分布（比如"每个目标被攻击的概率各是多少"），标准损失是交叉熵 (cross-entropy)。它问一个问题——

    When the model outputs a probability distribution (say, attack probability per target), the standard loss is cross-entropy. It asks one question —

    "真实发生的事，在你的分布里概率大吗？""How much probability did you give to what actually happened?"

    q = 真实分布（加权），q̂ = 模型分布（被打分）。真实集中在哪，就看你给那里的概率有多大。q = true distribution (the weighting), q̂ = model distribution (being scored). Wherever truth concentrates, it checks the probability you gave it.

    自己算一个例子：三个目标，真实攻击分布 q = (1, 0, 0)（确定打目标 1）；模型预测 q̂ = (0.5, 0.3, 0.2)。交叉熵 = −(1·log 0.5 + 0·log 0.3 + 0·log 0.2) = −log 0.5 ≈ 0.69。真实目标只分到一半概率，就罚 log 2。

    Compute one yourself: three targets, true distribution q = (1, 0, 0) (certain attack on target 1); model says q̂ = (0.5, 0.3, 0.2). CE = −(1·log 0.5 + 0 + 0) = −log 0.5 ≈ 0.69. Giving the true target only half the probability costs log 2.

    预测越准（q̂ 在真实处越接近 1），CE 越接近 0；分布"错得越偏"，CE 越大——q̂ 给真实事件的概率越小，−log 越急剧膨胀。

    The better calibrated q̂ (closer to 1 where truth is), the closer CE gets to 0; the more badly skewed the prediction, the larger CE grows — −log explodes as the probability you gave the truth shrinks.

    两个易混点：Two easy confusions:
    ① CE 的最小值不是 0"除非预测完美"——它下界是 0，且只在 q̂ = q 时取到。② CE 与 KL 散度只差一个常数（q 的熵）：最小化 CE ≡ 最小化 KL(q‖q̂)，所以"匹配分布"和"逼近分布"是一回事。 (1) CE's minimum is 0 only at the perfect prediction q̂ = q. (2) CE differs from KL divergence by a constant (the entropy of q): minimizing CE ≡ minimizing KL(q‖q̂) — 'matching the distribution' and 'approximating it' are the same task.
    你可能会问：log 底数是几？You might ask: which log base?

    无所谓——只差常数倍（e 底 ≈ 1.44 × 2 底），不影响"哪个更好"。论文和惯例用自然对数。本站所有 log 都是自然对数。

    Doesn't matter — bases differ by a constant factor (ln vs log2 ≈ ×1.44), never changing which prediction scores better. The paper uses natural log; so does this site.

    General theory · kp-gradient-descent一般理论 · 知识点 kp-gradient-descent

    梯度下降：浓雾下山Gradient descent: descending a mountain in fog

    想象你在一座山上，浓雾浓到三米外什么都看不见。你的目标：下到谷底。你看不到山的全貌——你唯一拥有的信息是脚下的坡度：往哪个方向踩，地势在升高；反方向，在降低。

    You are on a mountain in fog so thick you cannot see three meters. Your goal: reach the valley floor. The mountain's full shape is hidden — your only information is the slope under your feet: which way the ground rises, and therefore which way it falls.

    理性的做法朴素得可笑：感受一下哪个方向在下坡，朝那个方向迈一小步；再感受，再迈步。重复一万次。"梯度下降"这四个字说的就是这件事——蒙着眼睛，靠脚底的坡度，一小步一小步走下山。机器学习里所有的"训练"，底层都是这一万步。

    The rational move is laughably simple: feel which way is downhill, take a small step that way; feel again, step again; repeat ten thousand times. 'Gradient descent' is exactly this — blindfolded, following the slope under your feet, one small step at a time. Every 'training' in machine learning is these ten thousand steps at heart.

    把比喻翻译成数字Translating the metaphor into numbers

    山 = 损失函数（上一卡：给"错"打分的规则）；你的位置 = 模型的参数（可调的旋钮）；坡度 = 损失对参数的梯度（哪个方向旋，分数涨）；步子大小 = 学习率。写成一行更新公式：

    The mountain = the loss function (last card's error-scorer); your position = the model's parameters (adjustable knobs); the slope = the gradient of the loss with respect to the parameters; the step size = the learning rate. One line:

    θ = 参数（你在山上的位置）；∇L(θ) = 此处的坡度（上升方向，所以减号=往下坡走）；η = 步长。θ = parameters (where you stand); ∇L(θ) = local slope (the uphill direction — hence the minus); η = step size.

    亲手走两步（无山可爬就演算）：损失 L(w) = w²（一只碗，谷底在 w = 0）。你站在 w = 3，步长 η = 0.2。第一步：此处坡度 = 2×3 = 6，新位置 = 3 − 0.2×6 = 1.8。第二步：坡度 = 2×1.8 = 3.6，新位置 = 1.8 − 0.72 = 1.08。注意两件事：你确实在下山（损失 9 → 3.24 → 1.17）；步子自己变小了——因为越靠近谷底，坡越缓，同样的 η 走出的步子自然越短。

    Walk two steps by hand: loss L(w) = w² (a bowl, bottom at w = 0). You stand at w = 3, step size η = 0.2. Step one: slope = 2×3 = 6; new position = 3 − 0.2×6 = 1.8. Step two: slope = 3.6; new = 1.8 − 0.72 = 1.08. Notice two things: you are descending (loss 9 → 3.24 → 1.17), and the steps shrink on their own — near the bottom the slope flattens, so a fixed η takes shorter steps.

    步长的两难：The step-size dilemma: 步子太大——一步跨过谷底落到对岸更高处，越走越高（发散）；步子太小——安全但要走一万年。实践中"多大算合适"没有公式答案，靠在验证数据上试——这也是为什么训练模型像手艺活。 Too large — one step crosses the valley and lands higher on the far side (divergence); too small — safe but ten thousand years to the bottom. There is no formula for 'just right'; it is tuned on validation data — which is why training feels like craft.
    常见误解：Common misconception: "梯度下降保证找到最低点。"浓雾里你只能保证走到你所在盆地的谷底。如果山区有多个盆地（"非凸"地形），从东坡出发和从西坡出发可能到达完全不同的谷——出发点决定命运。全局保证只在"整座山只有一只碗"（凸）时成立。 'Gradient descent guarantees the lowest point.' In fog you only reach the bottom of your own basin. If the range has multiple basins ('nonconvex' terrain), starting east vs west can end in different valleys — your start decides your fate. A global guarantee exists only when the whole range is one bowl (convexity).
    你可能会问：真实训练几百万参数，怎么"感受坡度"？You might ask: with millions of parameters, how is the slope 'felt'?

    靠反向传播：用微积分的链式法则，把"最终损失对每个参数的坡度"从输出层一路算回输入层——一次前向 + 一次反向 = 所有参数各自的坡度。这是深度学习能运转的机械核心，本项目的知识表里有它的专题。

    Via backpropagation: the chain rule propagates 'how the final loss slopes with each parameter' from the output layer back to the input — one forward and one backward pass give every parameter's slope. This mechanism is what makes deep learning run at all.

    检查你自己（一般理论）Check yourself (general theory)

    TRANSFER迁移：浓雾比喻里，"浓雾"对应机器学习里的什么？Transfer: in the fog metaphor, what does the fog correspond to?

    本文如何用它：How this paper uses it: 下一卡：下山要"损失可微"，而统计学还有另一条老路通向同一座山谷——最大似然。 Next card: descending requires a differentiable loss, while statistics offers an older road to the same valley — maximum likelihood.
    In this paper · kp-gradient-descent本文用法 · 知识点 kp-gradient-descent

    梯度下降：顺着下坡走Gradient descent: walk downhill

    有了损失，怎么压低它？梯度下降 (gradient descent) 的想法一句话：对损失求梯度（坡道方向），朝下坡挪一小步：

    Given a loss, how do you push it down? Gradient descent in one line: take the gradient of the loss (the uphill direction), step the other way:

    θ = 模型参数，∇L = 损失的梯度，η (eta) = 学习率（步长）。重复千万次，损失滑向低谷。θ = model parameters, ∇L = gradient of the loss, η (eta) = learning rate (step size). Repeat millions of times and the loss slides into a valley.

    动手 · 点"走一步"，看小球下坡Hands-on · step the ball downhill
    损失曲线是碗，小球是当前参数。先预测：接近谷底时每步距离变大还是变小？The curve is the loss, the ball is the current parameter. Predict: near the bottom, do steps get longer or shorter?
    w = 0.00 · loss损失 = 4.00 · steps已走 0

    为什么步子在变小？梯度大小正比于坡度——碗底附近坡度趋平，同样的学习率走出的步子自然变小。这就是 η 可以保持常数的原因。

    Why do steps shrink? Step length is η × |gradient|; near the bottom the slope flattens, so constant η yields shrinking steps. That is why η can stay fixed.

    常见误解：Common misconception: 梯度下降找到的是"当前出发的这个碗里的低点"。曲线有两个碗（第 53 卡会遇到）时，从左边出发可能永远到不了更深的右边——非凸的麻烦正在这，论文为此专门造了工具。 Gradient descent finds the bottom of whichever bowl you started in. With two bowls (card 53), starting left may never reach the deeper right — that is the nonconvexity trouble, and the paper builds special tools for it.
    你可能会问：学习率 η 怎么选？You might ask: how do you pick η?

    太大：一步跨过谷底来回震荡甚至发散；太小：训练慢到无法接受。实践用验证集调，或自适应方法（Adam 等）。本文实验里两阶段方法调了学习率而 GF 用同样配置——对比公平性在卡 41 详谈。

    Too large: overshoot, oscillate, diverge. Too small: glacial training. In practice: tune on a validation set, or use adaptive methods (Adam…). In the paper's experiments both families share the same tuning budget — fairness discussed in card 54.

    General theory · kp-mle一般理论 · 知识点 kp-mle

    最大似然估计：一枚可疑的硬币Maximum likelihood: a suspicious coin

    你的朋友递来一枚硬币："我赌它有问题。"你掷了 10 次：7 次正面，3 次反面。现在他问："你觉得正面朝上的概率到底是多少？"

    A friend hands you a coin: 'I suspect it's rigged.' You flip it 10 times: 7 heads, 3 tails. Now he asks: 'So what do you think the true heads probability is?'

    你的直觉会脱口而出"0.7 吧"。你刚刚凭直觉完成了一次最大似然估计。现在把这个直觉讲成道理——为什么 0.7 比 0.5 更说得通？把三个候选值分别代入"10 次里出 7 次正面"的概率公式（二项分布），算出每个"世界观"下这批数据出现的可能性：

    Your gut says '0.7, obviously.' You just did a maximum likelihood estimate by intuition. Now make the intuition rigorous — why is 0.7 more defensible than 0.5? Plug candidate values into the probability of '7 heads in 10 flips' and compare how plausible the data is under each worldview:

    候选世界观 θCandidate θ这个硬币掷出 7 正 3 反的概率Pr(7 heads in 10 | θ)读法Reading
    0.5（公平硬币）≈ 0.117还行，但不是最解释数据的plausible, not the best explanation
    0.3≈ 0.009严重不符——这样的硬币很难掷出 7 正poor — such a coin rarely gives 7 heads
    0.7≈ 0.267最说得通——就是它了the most plausible explanation

    最大似然估计 (MLE) 就是把这张表系统化：固定已看到的数据，沿参数轴扫一遍，取"最能让数据出现"的那个参数值。公式只有一行：。argmax 读作"让后面达到最大的那个取值"。

    Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) systematizes that table: fix the data you saw, sweep the parameter axis, keep the value that makes the data most probable. One line: — argmax reads 'the value making the following maximal'.

    两个一劳永逸的事实：Two facts that pay forever: ① 对"硬币/骰子"这类计数问题，MLE 恰好等于经验频率（7/10 = 0.7；骰子 1 点出现 20/60 次 → 1/3）——直觉与公式在此握手。② 对"高斯噪声下的回归"，MLE 恰好等于最小二乘。机器学习一大半的损失函数都在暗中做 MLE——包括你两卡前学的交叉熵。 (1) For counting problems like coins and dice, MLE is exactly the empirical frequency (7/10 = 0.7; face-1 in 20 of 60 rolls → 1/3) — intuition and formula shake hands. (2) For regression under Gaussian noise, MLE is exactly least squares. Over half of ML's losses secretly do MLE — including cross-entropy from two cards ago.
    阿喀琉斯之踵：The Achilles heel: MLE 只看"这批数据"，数据一少就变得极端。掷 3 次全是正面 → MLE 宣布"正面概率 = 100%，反面不可能"——一叶障目。数据饥饿 + 参数多的场景（比如这篇论文：几百条攻击记录要撑起几百个参数）里，纯粹的 MLE 会说出荒谬的自信。后文会看到论文怎么处理它。 MLE trusts only the data at hand, so scarce data makes it extreme. Three flips, all heads → MLE declares 'heads = 100%, tails impossible' — blind to one leaf. In hungry-data + many-parameter settings (like this paper: a few hundred attack records holding up hundreds of parameters), pure MLE speaks with absurd confidence. Watch how the paper handles it.
    你可能会问：似然和概率到底差在哪？You might ask: likelihood vs probability?

    同一张表，两种读法。概率的读法：θ 固定（已知硬币公平），问"7 正 3 反"多常见。似然的读法：数据固定（7 正 3 反已到手），问"哪个 θ 最让它们常见"。固定谁、移动谁，就是全部区别。

    Same table, two readings. Probability: θ fixed (a fair coin), how common is '7 heads'? Likelihood: data fixed (7 heads in hand), which θ makes them most common? What is held fixed versus varied is the entire difference.

    检查你自己（一般理论）Check yourself (general theory)

    UNDERSTAND掷 2 次全正面，MLE 说 θ = 1.0。这个估计毛病在哪？Two flips, both heads: MLE says θ = 1.0. What's wrong with this estimate?

    APPLY数值题：骰子掷 60 次，'1' 出现 20 次。P(掷出 1) 的 MLE ≈ ?（三位小数）Numeric: a die rolled 60 times shows '1' twenty times. MLE of P(rolling 1) ≈ ? (3 decimals)

    TRANSFER迁移：垃圾邮件过滤器统计"包含'中奖'一词的邮件里，多少比例是垃圾"。这个比例是怎么来的？Transfer: a spam filter tracks 'of emails containing WINNER, what fraction are spam'. Where does that fraction come from?

    本文如何用它：How this paper uses it: 下一卡：期望效用——把"每种结果的概率"和"每个结果的好坏"拧在一起的那把螺丝刀。 Next card: expected utility — the screwdriver that twists probabilities and payoffs together.
    In this paper · kp-mle本文用法 · 知识点 kp-mle

    最大似然估计：让观测最可能的参数MLE: the parameter that makes the data most plausible

    最大似然估计 (Maximum Likelihood Estimation, MLE) 的问题设定永远一样：你有一个带未知参数 θ 的概率模型，手里有一批观测数据。MLE 问——

    The setup for Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) is always the same: a probability model with unknown parameter θ, plus observed data. MLE asks —

    "取哪个 θ，能让'看到手头这批数据'这件事的概率最大？""Which θ makes the observed data most probable?"

    两秒的例子：抛一枚硬币 10 次出现 7 次正面。哪个正面概率 θ 最能让这件事发生？把 θ = 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 分别代入二项分布算概率——0.7 赢。MLE 说 θ̂ = 0.7，恰好也是频率本身（一般规律：伯努利的 MLE = 经验频率）。

    A two-second example: a coin lands heads 7 of 10 flips. Which heads-probability θ makes this most probable? Plug θ = 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 into the binomial probability — 0.7 wins. MLE says θ̂ = 0.7, exactly the empirical frequency (a general fact for Bernoulli models).

    MLE 在本文出场两次：MLE appears twice in this paper: 第一次是老用法——图 1b 用 MLE 从攻击记录估计覆盖权重 w，收敛很快；第二次是新用法、本文的巧思——用 MLE 反解每个目标的价值 φ(yi)，从而模拟对手对任何覆盖的反应（第 47 卡一步步带你算）。 First the old use — Fig 1b estimates the coverage weight w from attack records by MLE, converging fast. Second the novel use — the paper's trick — inverting MLE to recover each target's value φ(yi), enabling simulation of the adversary's response to any coverage (card 47 walks the computation).
    常见误解：Common misconception: MLE 给的是"最能让数据出现的参数"，不是"参数最可能是多少"——后者是贝叶斯后验。数据很少时 MLE 会过拟合：20 个目标只有 5 次攻击记录，MLE 会把大量目标的价值钉死在极端值上。数据饥饿，正是这篇论文全部故事的起点。 MLE gives "the parameter that best explains the data", not "the most plausible parameter" — that is the Bayesian posterior. With little data MLE overfits: 20 targets, 5 attack records, and MLE pins many target values at extremes. Data hunger is where this entire paper begins.
    你可能会问：似然和概率差在哪？You might ask: likelihood vs probability?

    数值同一个东西，问的问题相反：概率="参数已知，数据出现的可能性"；似然="数据已到手，哪个参数最说得通"。固定数据、移动参数看谁高——就是在读似然函数。

    Numerically the same object, opposite questions: probability = "given the parameter, how likely is the data"; likelihood = "given the data, which parameter reads most plausible". Fix data, vary the parameter, and you are reading the likelihood function.

    Paper §2 · Setting

    把巡逻问题写成一行数学Writing the patrol problem in one line of math

    一个 Stackelberg 安全博弈 (SSG) 是四件套 ：

    A Stackelberg security game (SSG) is a four-part tuple :

    符号Symbol含义Meaning本文中的取值In this paper
    T目标集合Set of targets公园的 8 或 24 个巡护格8 or 24 patrol zones
    ud防守方效用：i 被得手时 ≤ 0Defender utility if target i falls: ≤ 0负值，如 −5（物种越关键损失越大）Negative, e.g. −5 (rarer species hurt more)
    ua攻击方效用：i 得手时 ≥ 0Attacker utility if target i falls: ≥ 0盗猎者的私人收益The poacher's private gain
    Cd防守策略的约束集Constraints on the defense strategy典型如 Σpi ≤ 资源数、排班约束Typically Σpi ≤ resources, scheduling rules

    一条关键会计规则：攻击被覆盖的目标时，双方收益都是 0——失败不罚款、成功不颁奖，世界只是恢复原状。整个博弈只剩"被得手的目标"在产生效用。

    One crucial accounting rule: when the attacked target is covered, both players get 0 — no fine for failing, no bonus for catching; the world simply resets. Only successfully-attacked targets generate utility.

    符号习惯（论文原文）：ud : T → ℝ≤0、ua : T → ℝ≥0。防守选覆盖向量 p 满足 Cd；对手的攻击函数 q 输出每个目标的攻击概率。

    Notation (verbatim from the paper): ud : T → ℝ≤0, ua : T → ℝ≥0. The defender picks coverage p satisfying Cd; the adversary's attack function q assigns an attack probability to each target.

    常见误解：Common misconception: ud 和 ua 不是彼此的镜面。目标可以"对盗猎者值钱、对公园不金贵"，也可以反过来。两张效用表的相关结构是第 38–39 卡定理 1 与定理 2 结论相反的原因——先埋颗种子。 ud and ua are not mirror images. A target can be precious to poachers yet unimportant to the park, or vice versa. The correlation structure of the two tables is why Theorems 1 and 2 (cards 38–39) point in opposite directions — a seed to plant now.

    Formula card · Eq. (1)

    DEU：防守方期望效用——全篇最重要的公式DEU: the defender's expected utility — the paper's central formula

    逐符号拆解Every symbol, unpacked

    片段Fragment读法Reading
    在满足约束的所有覆盖里挑最好的——"资源怎么分"的全部自由都在这个 max 里Pick the best coverage among all satisfying the constraints — the whole freedom of 'how to allocate' lives in this max
    目标 i 处于未覆盖状态的概率——攻击恰好成功的机会Probability target i is uncovered — the chance an attack there succeeds
    对手真会来打 i 的概率——注意它依赖 p！你一动，全盘重新分Probability the adversary actually attacks i — note it depends on p! Move your coverage and the whole distribution reshuffles
    后果：目标 i 的分量，非正值The consequence if i falls: non-positive
    把所有目标的长期账算总——DEU 是系统指标，不是逐格独立小仗Sum the long-run ledger over all targets — DEU is a system metric, not per-cell skirmishes

    已验证数值实例（手算核对）A verified numeric example (hand-checked)

    两个目标，ud = (−4, −2)，对手攻击概率 q = (0.5, 0.5)（与 p 无关时先简化），p = (0.5, 0)：DEU = (1−0.5)×0.5×(−4) + (1−0)×0.5×(−2) = −2.0。若把 p 改成 (1, 0)：DEU = 0 + 0.5×(−2) = −1.0。覆盖更有价值的目标 1，收益翻倍。

    Two targets, ud = (−4, −2), q = (0.5, 0.5) (independent of p, for simplicity), p = (0.5, 0): DEU = (1−0.5)×0.5×(−4) + (1−0)×0.5×(−2) = −2.0. With p = (1, 0): DEU = 0 + 0.5×(−2) = −1.0. Covering the more valuable target doubles the outcome.

    认出它了吗？Recognize it? 求和号里的每一项 ，就是第 8 卡那个"防守方单哨点特例"——期望效用的一般定义（概率×效用求和）落在目标 i 上的样子。Eq. (1) 没有发明新东西：它只是把特例对所有目标加总，而且仍然只是防守方这一个主体的期望效用（攻击方那份在第 29 卡的 argmax 里）。 Each term in the sum, , is exactly card 8's 'defender single-post special case' — the general definition of expected utility (probability × utility, summed) landing on target i. Eq. (1) invents nothing new: it sums the special case over all targets, and it is still the expected utility of one single agent — the defender (the attacker's share lives in card 29's argmax).
    为什么这是全篇最重要的公式？Why is this THE formula of the paper? 三个理由：①它是防守方的目标函数（max 的对象）；②它出现在两阶段方法的"第二阶段"和端到端方法的"损失"里——两条路线最后都要回到它；③它内部藏着整个故事的张力：q 依赖 p（攻击转移），而 q 又是未知的、要学的。 Three reasons: (1) it is the defender's objective — the thing being maximized; (2) it appears in the two-stage pipeline's second stage AND as the end-to-end loss — both routes return here; (3) it contains the whole story's tension: q depends on p (attack transfer), and q is unknown, to be learned.

    你来当巡逻队长You are the patrol captain now

    纸面到此为止。下面是一局完整的 Stackelberg 安全博弈：8 个巡护格（圆圈）、3 支巡逻队，对手是 SUQR 盗猎者（覆盖惩罚 w = −4，目标吸引力 φ 暂时保密）。点击任意圆圈循环设置覆盖率：0 → 0.25 → 0.5 → 0.75 → 1 → 0。每格下方的小柱是模型算出的攻击概率 qi——随你的布防实时变化。

    Enough paper. Below is a complete Stackelberg security game: 8 patrol zones (circles), 3 squads, a SUQR poacher (coverage penalty w = −4; target attractiveness φ hidden). Click any circle to cycle its coverage: 0 → 0.25 → 0.5 → 0.75 → 1 → 0. The small bars under each zone are the model's attack probabilities qi — live-updating as you deploy.

    已用资源：Resources used: 0.00 / 3 · DEU = —

    任务清单（每个任务都有它的"为什么"）Tasks (each with its 'why')

    1
    裸奔基线。Do-nothing baseline. 什么都不设防，记下 DEU。为什么？——你得知道"什么都不做"值多少，后面的每一点进步才有参照系。 Deploy nothing; note the DEU. Why? You must know what 'nothing' is worth before any progress means anything.
    2
    直觉布防。Intuitive deployment. 不许看 φ，凭感觉点 3 份覆盖。为什么？——这模拟"没有模型、只靠经验"的巡逻队长，也是 UNIF 基线代表的世界。 Without revealing φ, place 3 squads by gut. Why? This simulates the experience-only captain — the world UNIF stands for.
    3
    揭示 φ 再布防。Reveal φ, redeploy. 观察 q 柱涌向哪里，重新分配。为什么？——这一步你扮演"对手模型已学准"的防守方：知道口味后，同样 3 份资源能值多少钱。 Watch where the q bars flood, then redeploy. Why? You are now the defender whose adversary model learned well — what are 3 squads worth with tastes known?
    4
    对抗参考最优。Beat the reference optimum. 点"参考最优解"对比。为什么？——最优解往往不是把资源堆在吸引力最高的目标上，而是留一部分"看住第二梯队"。回到期望损失公式的三个因子想想为什么。 Compare with the reference optimum. Why? The optimum usually does NOT pile onto the most alluring targets — it keeps a reserve watching the second tier. Think about the three factors of expected loss.
    注意一个微妙现象：你覆盖一个目标时，它的 q 柱会塌下去，但攻击压力没有消失——被挤到了别处（q 是归一化的）。这就是安全博弈著名的攻击转移效应：防守永远是全盘棋，不是逐格的独立小仗。 A subtle phenomenon: cover a target and its q bar collapses — but the attack pressure has not vanished; it was squeezed elsewhere (q is normalized). This is the famous attack transfer effect: defense is one whole-board game, never per-cell skirmishes.
    你可能会问：这里的"最优"是全局最优吗？You might ask: is the reference optimum truly optimal?

    它来自覆盖率网格（0.25 步长、总量 ≤ 3）的穷举搜索，对这个 8 目标玩具博弈足够精确。论文里连续覆盖空间用非凸优化求解器求解——如何对求解器求导，正是定理 4（第 53 卡）的主角。

    It comes from exhaustive search over the coverage grid (0.25 steps, total ≤ 3) — exact enough for this 8-target toy game. The paper's continuous coverage space needs a nonconvex solver — and differentiating through one is precisely Theorem 4's job (card 53).

    Paper §2 · The attacker spectrum

    对手的两副面孔：理性 vs 有限理性The attacker's two faces: rational vs boundedly rational

    DEU 里的 q 有两种写法，论文正文都给出了——

    The q in DEU comes in two forms, both given in §2:

    完全理性对手The perfectly rational attacker

    他眼里的目标价值是"得手收益 × 成功概率"=(1−pj)ua(j)——防守折扣后的剩余价值。argmax 型：全押最优，别的看都不看。His perceived value is success-discounted: (1−pj)ua(j). Argmax-type: all-in on the best, nothing else.

    有限理性对手（QR）The boundedly rational attacker (QR)

    λ→∞ 时收敛到理性版本；λ 有限时给出"大部分打最爱、偶尔逛别处"的真实画像。Converges to the rational case as λ→∞; at finite λ it paints the realistic picture: mostly the favorite, occasionally wandering.

    为什么论文需要一个"平滑版"理性？Why does the paper need the smooth version? 两个原因，都贯穿全文：①可学习性——argmax 型对手永远只暴露他的第一名，随机性让完整偏好排序在重复对局中显露（第 47 卡的反演全靠它）；②可微性——exp 光滑，防守优化才能求梯度（定理 4）。 Two reasons, both recurring: (1) learnability — an argmax attacker only ever reveals his #1; stochasticity exposes the whole preference ranking over repeated play (card 47's inversion lives on this); (2) differentiability — exp is smooth, which is what lets the defense optimization be differentiated (Theorem 4).
    常见误解：Common misconception: 理性对手衡量的不是 ua(j) 本身，而是 (1−pj)ua(j)。忘了防守折扣，argmax 就会指错目标——这是推导中最高频的错误。 The rational attacker weighs (1−pj)ua(j), not ua(j) alone. Forget the coverage discount and the argmax points at the wrong target — the most frequent slip in derivations.

    还记得第 16 卡的分工吗——w（覆盖惩罚）全局通用、φ（目标价值）逐目标难学？图 1b 就是"分工声明"的证据：w 的 MLE 估计在十来局观测内就贴住真值 −4。这意味着：一旦在某个博弈里学出 w，可以直接迁移给同一对手的所有后续博弈。学习的全部火力可以集中在 φ 上。

    Paper §2 · Learning in SSGs

    真正的难题：q 是未知的The real problem: q is unknown

    DEU 公式里藏着一个被我们假装看不见的东西：——对手的攻击函数未知。没人发放盗猎者行为说明书。论文把这一项从"已知"变成"要从数据里学"，正式定义带潜在攻击函数的 SSG 实例 (SSG-LA)：

    Inside DEU hides something we pretended not to see: — the adversary's attack function is unknown. Nobody hands out poacher manuals. The paper turns this from 'known' into 'learned from data', defining an SSG instance with a latent attack function (SSG-LA):

    • q（潜在攻击函数）：特征+覆盖 → 攻击概率的真实映射，防守方永远观察不到它本身，只看到行为后果(latent attack function): features+coverage → true attack probabilities; never observed directly, only through behavior
    • Dtrain：训练博弈，每局 ——目标集、特征、观测到的攻击 A、防守效用、当时的覆盖: training games, each — targets, features, observed attacks A, defender utilities, historical coverage
    • Dtest：测试博弈，每局 ——只有目标和特征，要你给覆盖: test games, each — targets and features only; you must produce coverage

    反盗猎语境：训练局 = 巡护队去过的区域（所以有攻击记录）；测试局 = 整个公园（含从未巡过的角落）。从"去过的地方"学对手口味，推广到"没去过的地方"——彻底的泛化问题，论文假设博弈独立同分布抽取。

    In anti-poaching terms: training games = zones patrols visited (hence attack records); test games = the whole park (including never-patrolled corners). Learn tastes from visited zones, generalize to unvisited ones — pure generalization, with games drawn i.i.d.

    被动学习：别无选择的选择。Passive learning: the choice you don't get to make. 文献的分界线：主动学习——防守方故意变换巡逻"试探"对手；被动学习——只能用历史数据。论文选被动，理由很现实：公园积攒的历史数据远超短期可主动收集的量，而管理机构极少允许"为试探盗猎者而故意不巡某区"。 The literature's dividing line: active — the defender varies patrols to probe; passive — history only. The paper goes passive, for real reasons: accumulated history dwarfs what could be actively collected, and no park service lets you leave zones unpatrolled just to probe.

    Formula card · Eq. (3)

    式 (3)：学的是"策略函数"，不是"一次覆盖"Eq. (3): learning a policy, not one coverage vector

    逐符号拆解Every symbol, unpacked

    片段Fragment读法Reading
    策略函数：输入一个新博弈（目标和特征），输出覆盖向量。学习的产物是 x 这个函数，不是某一个 pA policy: takes a new game (targets, features), outputs coverage. What gets learned is the function x, not one vector p
    对测试博弈分布取期望——不是在某一局上好，而是在"整个公园的博弈流"上好Expectation over the test-game distribution — good not on one game but on the whole stream of games
    分号之后是真实攻击函数 q——它未知，这正是全部困难的来源After the semicolon: the TRUE attack function q — unknown, and the source of every difficulty

    对比式 (1)：式 (1) 是"给定 q，优化一次覆盖"；式 (3) 是"q 未知，学一个从特征到覆盖的策略，在测试分布上效用最大"。从优化问题升级为学习问题，一行之差。

    Contrast with Eq. (1): Eq. (1) optimizes one coverage given q; Eq. (3) learns a feature→coverage policy maximizing utility over the test distribution. From optimization to learning — the upgrade in one line.

    注意角标：Watch the subscript: 期望是对 Dtest 取的，但我们手里只有 Dtrain。整个方法的工程就是把"训练分布上可算的东西"变成"测试分布上想要的东西"——泛化差距全部压缩在这个替换里。 The expectation is over Dtest, but we only hold Dtrain. The whole method is the engineering of replacing 'computable on train' with 'wanted on test' — all of generalization squeezed into that substitution.

    Paper §2 · Two-stage

    两阶段方法：全世界在用的标准答案The two-stage approach: the world's standard answer

    论文图 2（原图）：上排两阶段，下排博弈聚焦。仔细看箭头——这将是第 49 卡的主角。Paper Fig. 2 (original): two-stage on top, game-focused below. Watch the arrows — they are the protagonist of card 49.

    面对未知 q，最自然的思路是拆成两步各司其职：

    Facing unknown q, the natural recipe splits the job in two:

    阶段一 · 预测Stage 1 · Predict
    交叉熵训练 q̂ 到最准train q̂ to maximal accuracy
    →
    阶段二 · 优化Stage 2 · Optimize
    把 q̂ 当真，解最优覆盖treat q̂ as truth, solve for coverage

    阶段一像多分类：目标=类别，输入=特征+历史覆盖，输出=预测攻击分布。损失用交叉熵（式 4，下一卡）。阶段二：对 q̂ 解式 (1) 的优化（式 5，再下一卡）。

    Stage 1 is multiclass classification: targets = classes, inputs = features + historical coverage, output = predicted attack distribution; loss = cross-entropy (Eq. 4, next card). Stage 2: solve Eq. (1)'s optimization against q̂ (Eq. 5, the card after).

    两阶段的哲学是模块化：预测归预测、优化归优化。真实优点——预测端可随意换成最强网络、吃任意特征，优化器独立升级。这是它统治领域的原因，也是它的魅力。

    The philosophy is modularity: prediction here, optimization there. Real virtues — swap in the strongest predictor, feed it any features, upgrade the optimizer independently. This is why it ruled the field, and why it is genuinely attractive.

    但请注意一个偷换：But notice a quiet substitution: 阶段一的损失是交叉熵——度量"预测像不像观测"；整个问题真正要的是 DEU——"防守方少损失多少"。两个目标之间的裂缝，就是这篇论文的全部。Part C 亲手撕开它。 Stage 1's loss is cross-entropy — 'how much does the prediction resemble the observations'; the problem truly wants DEU — 'how little does the defender lose'. The crack between these two objectives is this entire paper. Part C tears it open by hand.
    你可能会问：交叉熵有什么错？分类都用它。You might ask: what's wrong with cross-entropy? Everyone uses it.

    纯预测任务里它没错——甚至是合理最优。它"错"在场景：预测是手段，防守是目的。当你只在意下游决策时，为预测优化的模型可能把误差花在最不致命处，也可能花在最致命处——它完全不关心。

    For pure prediction it is fine — even optimal. It goes 'wrong' in context: prediction is a means, defense the end. When only the downstream decision matters, a prediction-optimized model may spend its errors where they are harmless — or where they are lethal. It does not care either way.

    UNDERSTAND图 2 里两阶段管线的"梯度死角"在哪个盒子？In Fig. 2's two-stage pipeline, where is the 'gradient dead-end'?

    TRANSFER迁移：你把两阶段的预测器换成更大的深度网络，什么时候能改善最终防守？Transfer: swapping in a bigger predictor helps the final defense when…?

    Formula card · Eq. (4)

    式 (4)：两阶段的"第一级火箭"Eq. (4): the two-stage pipeline's first-stage engine

    逐符号拆解 + 记号约定Every symbol, plus the notation convention

    符号Symbol读法Reading
    (hat 帽子)模型输出——"预测"。全文约定：帽子 = 模型的估计The model output — a prediction. Paper-wide: hats mark model estimates
    (tilde 波浪)经验攻击分布：观测到的频率。约定：波浪 = 来自数据的真值/经验量The empirical attack distribution from observed frequencies. Tildes mark empirical/ground-truth quantities
    目标 i 被观测到 Ai 次攻击，总共 |A| 次 → 频率即概率估计Target i took Ai observed attacks out of |A| total → frequency as probability estimate
    以真实频率加权、对模型给的 log 概率求平均——卡 13 交叉熵的直接应用Truth-weighted average of the model's log-probabilities — card 20's cross-entropy applied directly

    已验证数值实例：3 目标，观测攻击 A = (2, 0, 0)（|A|=2，全打目标 1）→ q̃ = (1, 0, 0)。模型 A 预测 q̂ = (0.5, 0.3, 0.2)：L = −1×ln 0.5 ≈ 0.69。模型 B 预测 (0.9, 0.05, 0.05)：L = −ln 0.9 ≈ 0.105。交叉熵强力奖励"把概率堆到实际发生处"。

    Verified numeric example: 3 targets, observed A = (2, 0, 0) (all attacks on target 1) → q̃ = (1, 0, 0). Model A predicts q̂ = (0.5, 0.3, 0.2): L = −ln 0.5 ≈ 0.69. Model B predicts (0.9, 0.05, 0.05): L = −ln 0.9 ≈ 0.105. Cross-entropy lavishly rewards piling probability where attacks actually landed.

    帽子和波浪谁更"真"？Which is 'truer' — hat or tilde? 都不真：q̂ 是模型猜想，q̃ 只是样本频率（一个局 5 次攻击，噪声巨大）。真正的 q 潜在幕后从未现身。整个两阶段就是把"逼近 q̃"当成了"逼近 q"——样本噪声和目标错位两笔账混在一笔里记。 Neither is true: q̂ is a model's guess, and q̃ is merely a sample frequency (5 attacks in a game — very noisy). The real q never appears. Two-stage conflates 'approximating q̃' with 'approximating q' — sample noise and objective mismatch booked in one ledger.

    Formula card · Eq. (5)

    式 (5)：一步安静的替换，全部问题所在Eq. (5): one quiet substitution, the whole problem

    逐字对比式 (3)：期望下标 Dtest 消失了（对单个测试局操作）；分号后的 q 换成了 q̂。就这两处。

    Diff against Eq. (3): the expectation over Dtest is gone (we operate on a single test game), and after the semicolon, q has been replaced by q̂. Those two changes, nothing else.

    这个替换就是"信任"：This substitution IS the act of trust: 第二阶段把 q̂ 当成真话——优化器对 q̂ 的每个误差全盘买单。而定理 1（第 37 卡）将证明：同样的误差，买单额可以差 2 倍以上。两阶段把误差的处理权完全交给了运气。 Stage two takes q̂ at face value — the optimizer pays full price for every error in it. Theorem 1 (card 38) will show the same errors can cost 2× apart. Two-stage hands the handling of error entirely to luck.

    公平地说——这个替换是所有预测+优化系统的默认动作，而且当 q̂ ≈ q 时它无伤大雅（误差 ε 的后果连续依赖 ε）。裂缝只在"后果不连续/方向敏感"时张开。什么时候张开？这正是 Part C 的定理要精确刻画的事。

    Fairness demands saying: this substitution is the default move of every predict-then-optimize system, and it is harmless when q̂ ≈ q (consequences depend continuously on ε). The crack opens only when consequences are discontinuous or direction-sensitive. When? That is precisely what Part C's theorems pin down.

    Paper §3 · Impact of two-stage on DEU

    亲手撕开裂缝：把论文的三目标例子算到底Tearing the crack open: the 3-target example computed to the end

    论文最重要的直觉来自一个玩具例子。设置：3 目标、1 份资源、防守方等值 ud = (−1,−1,−1)、完全理性对手，真实价值 z = (0.4, 0.4, 0.2)。一步步算——每一步你都能在草稿纸上跟上。

    The paper's most important intuition is a toy example. Setup: 3 targets, 1 resource, equal defender values ud = (−1,−1,−1), a perfectly rational attacker, true values z = (0.4, 0.4, 0.2). Compute step by step — follow along on paper.

    对手的最优反应。The adversary's best response. 理性对手攻击 argmaxj (1−pj)·zj——"覆盖折扣后的剩余价值"最大的目标。 The rational attacker hits argmaxj (1−pj)·zj — the largest coverage-discounted residual value.
    真最优覆盖 p*。The true optimal coverage p*. 若全防一个（如 p=(1,0,0)），对手打剩下的 0.4 → 损失 0.4。均衡技巧：把覆盖分给两个 0.4：p* = (0.5, 0.5, 0) → 各目标剩余 (0.5·0.4, 0.5·0.4, 1·0.2) = (0.2, 0.2, 0.2) 全并列 → 对手打谁都损失 0.2。最优损失 = −0.2。 Full-covering one target (say (1,0,0)) leaves the 0.4s exposed → loss 0.4. The balancing trick: split across the two 0.4s, p* = (0.5, 0.5, 0) → residuals (0.2, 0.2, 0.2), all tied → loss 0.2 whoever he hits. Optimal = −0.2.
    估计 A：错得离谱。Estimate A: spectacularly wrong. ẑ = (0.5, 0.5, 0.0)——前两个高估 25%，第三个低估 100%。对 ẑ 优化：均衡 (1−p)·0.5 两项 → pA = (0.5, 0.5, 0)。恰好就是真最优覆盖！真实损失 −0.2。 ẑ = (0.5, 0.5, 0.0) — overstates the first two by 25%, understates the third by 100%. Optimizing against ẑ: equalize the (1−p)·0.5 terms → pA = (0.5, 0.5, 0). Exactly the true optimal coverage! True loss −0.2.
    估计 B：几乎完美。Estimate B: nearly perfect. ẑ = (0.4−ε, 0.4−ε, 0.2+2ε)。微小误差让目标 3 "看起来最诱人" → 优化器全力压它：pB ≈ (0, 0, 1)。真实对手回头打任一 0.4 → 损失 −0.4。ε→0 也不好转。 ẑ = (0.4−ε, 0.4−ε, 0.2+2ε). The tiny error makes target 3 'look most attractive' → the optimizer piles onto it: pB ≈ (0, 0, 1). The true attacker turns to either 0.4 → loss −0.4. No improvement as ε→0.
    判决。The verdict. 同样"准确"（A 的 MSE 甚至更大）的两个模型，决策后果差整整一倍。原因：argmax 是分水岭——误差落在同侧毫无影响，跨过一点点就翻山。MSE 完全看不见分水岭在哪。 Two equally 'accurate' models (A's MSE is even larger), yet the decision outcomes differ by a factor of two. Why: the argmax is a watershed — errors on the same side change nothing, a hair across it flips the mountain. MSE cannot see where the watershed lies.
    你可能会问：argmax 相同的话两个估计就等价了吗？You might ask: if two estimates give the same argmax, are they equivalent?

    是——论文正文明确举了这种"误差无影响"的情形。关键在分水岭：同侧等价、跨界跳崖。均方误差对所有方向的误差一视同仁，而博弈只对"跨没跨"敏感。

    Yes — the paper itself notes such 'error without consequence' cases. It is all about the watershed: same side equivalent, across it a cliff. MSE weights all error directions equally; the game only cares whether you crossed.

    想一想：如果你是"上帝"，可以给两阶段方法一个误差方向偏好，该偏好是什么？（答案在下一卡定理 1）Think: if you were omniscient and could hand two-stage ONE bias about error direction, what should it be? (Answer: Theorem 1, next card.)
    Formula card · Theorem 1公式卡 · 定理 1

    定理 1：等值世界里，低估谁更好？Theorem 1: in the equal-value world, whom is it better to underestimate?

    设定（论文原文）：两目标、单资源、理性对手、防守方各目标等值（−1）；z₀ ≥ z₁ 为对手价值（非负、和为 1），防守方不知道；估计 (ẑ₀, ẑ₁) 的 MSE = ε²。

    Setup (verbatim): two targets, one resource, rational attacker, equal defender values (−1); z₀ ≥ z₁ the attacker's values (non-negative, summing to 1), unknown to the defender; the estimate (ẑ₀, ẑ₁) has MSE ε².

    MSE = ε² 的归一化估计只有两个：(z₀+ε, z₁−ε) 和 (z₀−ε, z₁+ε)——分别"低估高价值目标"和"低估低价值目标"。

    Only two normalized estimates have MSE ε²: (z₀+ε, z₁−ε) and (z₀−ε, z₁+ε) — respectively 'underestimate the high-value target' and 'underestimate the low-value target'.

    已验证数值实例（手算核对）Verified numeric check (hand-computed)

    z₀ = 0.7, z₁ = 0.3, ε = 0.05：

    z₀ = 0.7, z₁ = 0.3, ε = 0.05:

    低估高价值目标 (0.65, 0.35)：Underestimate the high-value target (0.65, 0.35): 按估计均衡布防 (1−p₀)·0.65 = (1−p₁)·0.35 → p = (0.65, 0.35)。真实对手看剩余：目标 0 剩 0.35×0.7=0.245，目标 1 剩 0.65×0.3=0.195 → 攻目标 0。损失 = 1−0.65 = 0.35 Equalize against the estimate: (1−p₀)·0.65 = (1−p₁)·0.35 → p = (0.65, 0.35). True residuals: target 0 has 0.35×0.7 = 0.245, target 1 has 0.65×0.3 = 0.195 → attacked on target 0. Loss = 1 − 0.65 = 0.35
    低估低价值目标 (0.75, 0.25)：Underestimate the low-value target (0.75, 0.25): 同法得 p = (0.75, 0.25)。真实剩余：0.25×0.7 = 0.175 vs 0.75×0.3 = 0.225 → 攻目标 1。损失 = 0.75 Same procedure: p = (0.75, 0.25). True residuals: 0.175 vs 0.225 → attacked on target 1. Loss = 0.75
    比率：The ratio: 0.75 / 0.35 ≈ 2.14 = (z₀+ε)/(z₁+ε) = 0.75/0.35 ✓ 公式与数字完全吻合。同样 MSE 的两个模型，一个让你多丢一倍地盘。 0.75 / 0.35 ≈ 2.14 = (z₀+ε)/(z₁+ε) ✓. Formula and numbers agree exactly. Two models with identical MSE; one costs you double the territory.
    直觉一句话：The intuition in one line: 低估高价值目标 → 对手扑向它 → 而你恰好重兵在守（"他以为我不在乎，而我在乎"）。低估低价值目标 → 对手偷袭你不设防的次要点。等值世界里：让对手的攻击落在你严阵以待的地方。 Underestimate the high-value target → the adversary rushes it → but you heavily guard it ('he thinks I don't care; I do'). Underestimate the low-value target → he raids the neglected second point. Equal-value world: let his attack land where you are entrenched.
    论文的证明草稿（一句话）：The paper's proof sketch (one sentence): "攻击者会攻击防守方低估的目标。防守方偏好后者——攻击者选中高价值目标——因为该目标覆盖更多，而失败成本两边相同。" 'The attacker attacks the target whose value the defender underestimates. The defender prefers the latter case — the high-value target — because it has more coverage, while successful attacks cost the same on both.'

    Formula card · Theorem 2公式卡 · 定理 2

    定理 2：只改一条假设，偏好整个反转Theorem 2: change one assumption, flip every preference

    设定：与定理 1 完全相同，只改一处——防守方效用变为 ud(i) = −zi（零和：你丢的就是他拿的）。MSE = ε² 的最好/最坏效用之比：

    Setup: identical to Theorem 1 except one change — the defender's utility becomes ud(i) = −zi (zero-sum: your loss is his gain). The best-to-worst utility ratio at MSE ε²:

    同样数字验证：z₀=0.7, z₁=0.3, ε=0.05。低估高价值目标 → 对手攻高价值目标 → 损失 0.35×0.7 = 0.245；低估低价值目标 → 损失 0.75×0.3 = 0.225。偏好反转了：现在你宁愿让对手去打便宜目标——"失败的低代价"盖过了"他得手更频繁"。比率 0.225/0.245 ≈ 0.918 ✓ 与公式一致。

    Same numbers: z₀ = 0.7, z₁ = 0.3, ε = 0.05. Underestimating the high-value target → attacked there → loss 0.35×0.7 = 0.245; underestimating the low-value target → loss 0.75×0.3 = 0.225. Preference reversed: now you prefer letting him raid the cheap target — 'the low cost of failure' outweighs 'he succeeds more often'. Ratio 0.225/0.245 ≈ 0.918 ✓ matches the formula.

    论文证明草稿原话：The paper's proof sketch, verbatim: "防守方偏好低估低价值目标的情形，诱导攻击者攻击它。失败的更低代价压过了对手更少被抓。" 'The defender prefers the case where she underestimates the attacker's value for the lower value target, inducing the attacker to attack it. The lower cost of failures outweighs the attacker getting caught less often.'
    一正一反合起来的数学宣言：Together, the two theorems declare: 哪种误差方向更好，取决于价值结构（等值？零和？相关方向？）——这些结构藏在数据里、因博弈而异，手写损失函数不可能预知。唯一诚实的做法：让效用损失自己出现在损失函数里。这就是 game-focused learning 的存在理由。 Which error direction is better depends on the value structure (equal? zero-sum? correlation direction?) — structure that lives in the data and differs per game. No hand-written loss can foresee it. The only honest move: let the utility loss appear inside the loss function. That is why game-focused learning exists.
